## The pipeline

```
tracker.api / create → tracker.scaffold → client drops into the household inbox → tracker.filer → tracker.scanner → tracker.reminder (on DRAFT_WEEKDAY) → tracker.view (the last step of every pass) → a person sends the draft
```

  - note: Every command prints one JSON object and returns an exit code - errors are JSON too, never a traceback. This is the only module the Electron app knows about. The create path validates rows with the same sentences the manifest's validation uses, and never leaves a half-built engagement behind: create_engagement() validates whole before a line is written, and on any later failure _undo_create() removes the folder first and then drops the store row in its own try, so a store that cannot be reached masks nothing and keeps no folder. list/priors use the same discovery as the scheduled run; create and rollover record the details from the wizard's client/link/due (rollover carries client, sender, firm and reminders, never last year's link or due); assign files a parked document by a person's choice and re-scans. unlock clears a stale lock; state carries the lock; templates carries each form's tax year and create names a new-client engagement from client, year and form when no name is given. create takes the tax year (calendar default) and shifts catalog rows to it; rollover writes Rolled From so the prior retires; priors report superseded_by. scan is run_engagement() with reminders=REMINDERS_NEVER - the app's button and the scheduled job make the same pass. The clients root comes from tracker.settings (settings, set-root, install-schedule commands); the wizard never writes Engagement Name, and reads the firm from settings.firm(). install-schedule works in the packaged app too. ENGAGEMENT_FLAG with nothing after it, or an empty folder, gets the same sentence as no flag; once a root is set the folder must lie under it. assign takes the lock twice on purpose (file, then re-scan). _vocab() hands the renderer every word it shows - the app carries no Python vocabulary of its own. Decision 55: containment is checked whenever a root is set (since decision 176 by the path's own parse, since decision 188 door.return_dir). Decision 67: a blank name falls back to the client's name sanitised. Decision 68: _tax_year() bounds the year on create and rollover alike, through manifest.check_tax_year() (decision 72). Decision 75: a pass made from the app is on the record the scheduled run leaves - _record_pass() appends the run log's line and redraws the status page. Decision 76: dismiss records that no request asks for a parked document and does not re-scan; _vocab() carries the decision under the key 'dismissed', not the word. Decision 77: unfile sends one filed document back for review. Decision 82: state's index rows carry evidence as data (_evidence_payload()). Decision 84: state carries 'review' - tracker.review.triage() over the rows state has already loaded, serialised by _triage_payload(). Decision 86: create records the wizard's catalog choice in the details; _state() ships it (_info_payload() is asdict() over EngagementInfo). Decision 89: _state() ships view: {state, path} from tracker.view.view_state(). Decision 91: paths['view'] is an .html file and _vocab()['view'] carries the button's own label. Decision 102: standing_rules() fills rule 2 from records.THE_RECORD; _state() calls filer.ensure() before reading the rows, so showing an engagement stays a read. DECISION 104: the edit command takes {items, engagement} from the editor, converts each row with manifest.item_from_fields() (each refusal naming its row), refuses any engagement key outside records.ENGAGEMENT_EDITABLE by name, and saves through manifest.save_rules(), replying with what changed, what was removed, which details moved, whether anything was recorded, and the warnings; a detail sent blank is cleared and one left out keeps its recorded value; a refusal is the usual error sentence and nothing is recorded. _state() gained 'rules' (the person's rows as stored - WITHOUT the keywords filings taught, so the editor never turns a taught word into a typed one), 'learned' (those keywords, keyed by the row's identifier) and 'warnings' (manifest.check_rules()); 'engagement' is the details from the record; paths lost the workbook. _vocab() gained 'columns' (each column's key, header and help from manifest.COLUMNS and COLUMN_HELP) and 'editor' (every word the editor shows, the details' fields with which are editable, the yes/no words, the two one-character values and the floors the number inputs take their minimum from); the check command and the Carried Forward sheet's name left with the things they named. DECISION 112: _state() reads store.document_seqs() once and hangs each row's sequence number beside it - on every 'index' row and on every 'review' item (_triage_payload takes the mapping) - never inside the row, because it is the record's bookkeeping and not a fact about the document. _cmd_assign, _cmd_dismiss and _cmd_unfile read spec['seq'] through _seq_of() and refuse a spec without one by NO_SEQ (a ManifestError): the app is always drawn from state, so a caller with no version is a caller with no view. _cmd_assign also computes the shortlist itself - _shortlist_now() reads the index, finds the row with filer.find_parked() and asks review.shortlist_for() over load_manifest() - and hands the identifiers to the filer, which imports neither; its payload gains 'overrode_shortlist'. This module is L4 and imports both, so the computation belongs here; the seq check under the lock is what makes a row that moved in between never get the handed-in shortlist written. DECISION 113: the unlearn command takes {identifier, keyword} from the editor, records one keyword_unlearned through manifest.unlearn_keyword() and then re-scans the engagement the way assign does (its own lock; a ScanLockedError becomes scan_note), because the request's rules just moved and a copy that passed only on that word should regress now rather than on Saturday. _vocab()['editor'] gained unlearn_label and unlearned_note - the button beside each taught keyword and the sentence after it - and the renderer types neither. Decision 117: _info_from_spec() and _info_payload() read records.DATE_FIELDS rather than naming the due date, _vocab()['editor']['date_fields'] tells the editor which boxes are dates, and rollover.with_default_dates() fills a blank Filing Deadline and Due Date from the form's own table on create and on rollover - so the reminder's ladder works without a person typing a date, and what a person typed is never written over. settings and set-root carry the firm's phone beside its name, and _vocab()['settings'] carries that box's label, its sentence and the number as recorded; _reminder_payload() takes the index rows state has already read, so the card shows the parked-file hold the draft day will. DECISION 110: _state() gains 'moved', its own list beside 'review' rather than a column on the index - one entry per FILE_MOVED row with the row's sequence number, the home the record put the copy at, where its bytes are now (None for a row whose bytes are nowhere under the firm's folder) and, only where the copy sits directly in Prepared under a name that belongs to a request (decision 168), which request that is, matched by scaffold.assign_files(), the same answer the filer and the scan read. The restore command is _cmd_restore(), the third review action beside assign and unfile and the only new one: it takes the row's seq like the others and returns what the put-back found (moved_home, copied_from_original, already_home, parked_as) beside the rewritten row. _vocab()['review_labels'] carries the card's every word - RESTORE_LABEL, KEEP_LABEL, SEND_TO_REVIEW_LABEL, MOVED_HEADING, MOVED_SUMMARY and MOVED_NOWHERE, the word for a copy that is nowhere - so the renderer types none of them, and _shortlist_now() finds a moved row too, because keep-it-here goes through the same assign command and the same picker. DECISION 114: _vocab()['review_labels'] carries the review card's second rendering too - ACCEPT_LABEL, SKIP_LABEL, OPEN_IN_LIST_LABEL, the two words the toggle between the renderings shows (CARD_MODE_LABEL, LIST_MODE_LABEL) and CARD_POSITION, the pattern the card's position line is filled from. The heading over the card's suggestion is SUGGESTED_HEADING, the list's own: one queue, one word for a suggestion. No command is added and no payload changes - the cards are a rendering of the 'review' list this module already ships, and Accept is the assign command the list's File it makes. Decision 123: that function is no longer defined here - it moved to tracker.rollover, beside the carry rule that clears the dates, because the module's command line built engagements without it; create and rollover import it and are otherwise unchanged. Decision 118 added the reminder and approve commands and everything the Reminder card shows. reminder reads the record and the draft file and regenerates the letter in memory at whatever stage the toggle stands on - no lock, nothing written, and a held reminder answers with no letter at all; approve takes the engagement lock, refuses a stale panel by the fingerprint of the text it showed, writes the shown text (or approves an edited file as it stands), sets any other draft aside and records one draft_approved event. _vocab() carries the card's every word, the four stages with the palette key each carries and where each spends its emphasis, and page.PALETTE itself, so the renderer types neither a word nor a colour; state's paths now name the draft file, because the shell opens only paths this map holds. Decision 126 added two commands and the sharing words: roll-household rolls every ticked return of a household's open year through rollover.roll_household() and answers with the rolled, the skipped with their sentences, the retired by their labels and the state of the first return it made; mark-shared records one sharing_confirmed event on the household's record under its lock, refusing while the inbox link is blank (SHARE_LINK_FIRST) because that is the one part of the checklist the tracker can see was done. SHARING_CHECKLIST, SHARING_HEADING, SHARING_NOTE, MARK_SHARED_LABEL, SHARED_ON_LINE, NOT_YET_SHARED_LINE and ROLLOVER_UNTICKED_NOTE are the API's words; create hands the filled checklist back with a household's FIRST return and with no other, and state['household'] carries shared_on and the same filled lines until it is given. propose-spellings is the twenty-third command and a read: it proposes the spellings a document might print one name in and records nothing, because what a return matches on is what a person ticked (decision 128). create refuses a return with nobody on it. Decision 129 added the feed words (FEEDS_LABEL, FEEDS_LINE, FED_BY_LINE, ADD_FEED_LABEL, FEED_WARNING, RETURN_WARNING, HAND_OVER_LABEL, NOT_FED), the feeds field on edit-household, the feeds and fed_by the household card is drawn from, and assign's optional target - which hands the document to a return the drop folder feeds and refuses any other by name. The review of that build added the hand-over modal's own two words (HAND_OVER_RETURN_LABEL, HAND_OVER_REQUEST_LABEL), which the page had been borrowing from the household heading and the editor's title, and gave _cmd_scan the same walk of the practice the card uses (_the_practice), so Run now sorts against the feed list exactly as the scheduled pass does rather than against the household's own returns alone; since decision 132 a root that cannot be walked is the runner's NO_PRACTICE, the reply's run error, and nothing is sorted. HANDED_OVER_LINE (review_labels.handed_over) is what the page says after a hand-over: the row here is released. Decision 131: _state() carries 'room' (room_for over the list it already loaded), 'room_note' (ROOM_SHORT filled, or '' - information the return's page shows, never a warning) and appends only ROOM_PARKS to the warnings; set-root answers 'short_of_room' - every working return short of room under the new root, in label order, with its numbers and filled sentences (one walk; the one time room is measured outside a pass) - and records the root regardless; the editor's save (_cmd_edit) refuses with PATH_TOO_LONG a CHANGED or new row whose canonical path passes 260, and never a row the person did not touch; install-schedule writes the job from settings_dir() and replies 'settings'. _vocab()['room'] holds the heading and the two sentences. Decision 137: create refuses a household folder that exists without a record (HOUSEHOLD_NOT_OURS, the misfit rule stated at the door) and makes every folder through fsio.make_new_folders(), so a failure undoes only what this call made (_undo_made); rollover the same. _engagement_dir() refuses when no clients root is set, and _engagement_dir() names a return by its place (four levels under the root, under a year) - a year or household folder is refused (NOT_A_RETURN) rather than read one level too high. _feeds_from_spec() refuses a feed whose household or return line the sanitiser would change. Review fixes: _undo_made() removes whole only the folders a call owns (its return, a household whose record it wrote) and a year folder only when empty; create drops a household's pre-137 non-web link with rollover.carried_link and returns link_dropped; the reminder card carries link_dropped. Decision 160: edit fills a key a row leaves out from the record's row of that identifier (_as_recorded(); absent means unchanged, as the details were; date_pattern_derived only with the pattern it describes), refuses a key outside _ROW_KEYS (RULE_FIELDS and extensions; UNKNOWN_COLUMN), requires the list's version (state's list_head; NO_LIST_HEAD, checked under the lock by save_rules) and refuses a save that takes a request holding filed documents off the list, removed or respelt other than by case (_refuse_taking_away_documents(), HOLDS_DOCUMENTS, from filer.documents_by_request()). The rename command (filer.rename_request) gives a request another identifier and moves its documents; its words are RENAME_* and RENAMED_NOTE in vocab.editor. The documents-held check runs as save_rules' check, inside the lock; HOLDS_DOCUMENTS points to Not Applicable. Decision 157: _moved_payload leaves out a row a person marked missing and carries gone (filer.both_gone) and the row's identifier; mark-missing takes a both-gone row's own identifier; restore accepts a Filed or parked row whose copy was deleted. Decision 176: every command reads stdin through _read_spec() - the bytes decoded as UTF-8, one JSON object or NOT_A_SPEC - because Windows reads a pipe in its ANSI code page and turned `Muñoz` into `MuÃ±oz` in a folder the client is shared. A path from the app is parsed by its place, never trusted: _return_dir() (four levels under the root, in the private tree, under a year) and _household_dir() (two levels) hand back the root joined with the resolved names, so no `..` reaches layout's text-reading helpers and a folder in the client tree - where a client can plant a journal - is never a prior or a household (NOT_A_RETURN, NOT_A_HOUSEHOLD); the old check that a path merely lay under the root is gone. Decision 177: rollover places next year under the household the prior sits in and the prior's own folder name, and _carried_payload() carries the prior's NAME_DISAGREES as `warning`. Decision 189 (E-11): scan's reply carries household (every other return of the household the pass touched: label, ok, error, skipped, warnings) and pass_warnings (the reader's path, a reader that could not start, the card, and _record_pass()'s own failures - LOG_NOT_WRITTEN, PAGE_NOT_WRITTEN - which it now returns rather than leaving on stderr); _record_pass() puts the pass's own sentences in the log and on the page. Decision 189: Run now is run_household() with the scheduled pass's own household budget, so it ends inside main.js's 30-minute kill and says OUT_OF_TIME instead of failing. Decision 187: _info_from_spec's date() refuses a date the records date rule refuses (1900-2100, a real calendar date), and the editor vocabulary carries 'maximums' (records.MAX_EXPECTED_COUNT, records.MAX_SIZE_KB) beside 'minimums', which app.js sets as the number inputs' max. Decision 188: _folder_name is layout.checked_name - one sentence wherever a household or return name is typed (create, a new return, a rolled return's name, a feed); a return is unique by the key within its household-year; feeds are compared by name_key; NOT_A_RETURN/NOT_A_HOUSEHOLD are layout's sentences. Decision 188 (part 2): _root is door.checked_root on every command (E-13) and _saved_root does the same where a missing root is an answer (list, priors, state, practice); list answers a refused saved root with needs_root, root_problem and the vocabulary; _return_dir/_household_dir are door.return_dir/household_dir; DoorError and LayoutError are answered as ManifestError is; the vocab carries path_kinds (PATH_KINDS) and shell.not_opened (SHELL_NOT_OPENED); each misfit carries 'where', its path below the root from layout.parts_below, so the page never computes it. Decision 188 (part 3): create refuses a typed household name that is, by the key, a household folder or record's name (DUPLICATE_HOUSEHOLD - pick it in the list; add a first name or a middle initial, then the city, never an identifier), a folder without a record (HOUSEHOLD_NOT_OURS) or a client folder no household owns (CLIENT_FOLDER_TAKEN); create by household_path, rollover and roll-household refuse a paused (or stopped) household. accept-folder-name (--engagement <return>, {seq, scope}) is the one action on a paused household: under the household's lock and each return's, judged by the household record's line count, it appends a household_changed {name} line and rules_changed {info} lines, each with ledger.ACCEPTED_KEY = FOLDER_NAME_ACCEPTED; refused for a year disagreement (YEAR_NOT_ACCEPTED) and, for a household, when a recorded original rests under a client folder of another name (ORIGINALS_UNDER_OLD_NAME). _household_payload carries 'pause' {sentence, scope, engagement, seq}; the vocab carries the action's label and help. Review of 188: every accept scope runs the originals check before writing and a return's accept never writes the household's name (M2); a year pause carries no scope, so no Accept button (S3); create by household_path and rollover ask registry.held_back (M3, S4). Decision 204: _triage_payload carries waits_for {target, label, requests [{identifier, document}], answers} or null, and waits_for_refused (NOT_FED with the claim's return name, or filer.requests_taking's refusal), from _waiting_payload(entry, fed) - the feed list read once per state and only when a row waits; assign with {original, seq, waiting: true} and no target or identifier goes to _hand_over_waiting(), which resolves the row's claim the same way and calls hand_over(also=, answers=, waiting=True); FILE_WHERE_IT_WAITS_LABEL is review_labels.file_where_it_waits.
- **`tracker/containers.py`** — Opens an email or a zip a client dropped, in memory, and hands back what was attached (decision 143): open_container(bytes, extension) gives each attachment's own name (safe_name(), a basename that cannot leave its folder) and bytes, and each part skipped with why (an inline picture, the message's own text, an attachment by reference or an OLE object); NotOpened carries the sentence a container parks with (reasons.CONTAINER_LOCKED, CONTAINER_DAMAGED, CONTAINER_EMPTY, CONTAINER_LIMIT). is_container() decides by the extension alone (.msg, .eml, .zip) - never magic bytes, because an .xlsx is a zip too.
  - CLI: `python -m tracker.containers`
  - constants: `MAX_DEPTH` = 2, `MAX_ATTACHMENTS` = 200, `MAX_TOTAL_MB` = 250, `MAX_RATIO` = 100, `MAX_SKIPPED` = 200, `NAME_MAX` = 255, `LIMIT_PACKING` = "a file inside is packed in a way only a person's zip program opens", `SKIP_INLINE` = 'inline image, shown in the message rather than attached', `SKIP_BODY` = "the message's own text, never saved", `SKIP_REFERENCE` = 'attached by reference: it holds a link, not the document', `SKIP_OLE` = 'an embedded object that would have to be run to be read', `SKIP_EMPTY` = 'attached with nothing in it', `SKIP_FOLDER` = 'a folder entry', `UNNAMED` = 'attachment {n}', `KIND_EMAIL` = 'an email', `KIND_ZIP` = 'a zip'
  - imports: `tracker/__init__.py`, `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/layout.py`, `tracker/reasons.py`
  - used by: `tracker/filer.py`
  - imports at call time: `tracker/page.py`
  - tested by: `tests/test_containers.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/child_readers.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`
  - note: Writes nothing, decides nothing about a folder and holds no file open: the filer checks the size ceiling, open_bounded() opens the container, and the filer writes what comes back. Decision 154: open_bounded(path) runs open_file() - read the file, open_container() - in the reading's child (content_check.in_a_child, the stop for a file, 600 s), handed over by reference through _CHILD_OPENER; the child hands back the Opened (plain data), a refusal's sentence, or the file's OSError, and open_bounded raises NotOpened for a refusal, the stop (READING_STOPPED) or a crash after 'started' (READING_CRASHED), and returns None for a child that never started (the filer records nothing and reopens it next pass). The suite opens in its own process unless content_check.READ_IN_A_CHILD is on. Three parsers on untrusted input: the standard library's email (policy.default; the one module under tracker/ that may import it, for parsing only - tests/test_layers.py names the exception and proves in a subprocess that importing this module reaches no mail client or network module beyond the socket and urllib the standard library's own helpers pull in), zipfile streamed through a counting read (never extract or extractall; names decoded as the zip marks them), and olefile for .msg (BSD-2-Clause, pinned; opened with DEFECT_INCORRECT raised; its sector-chain loops are bounded by the stream's size and its directory walk refuses a re-referenced entry). The limits are constants here, each with a test at its edge: MAX_DEPTH 2, MAX_ATTACHMENTS 200, MAX_TOTAL_MB 250 counted from the bytes actually produced, MAX_RATIO 100 per zip member, and MAX_SKIPPED 200 parts left inside (each is named on the record's line); a name on the record is cut to NAME_MAX, 255. The whole container is opened before anything is written, so a limit leaves nothing behind. A container nested past the depth, or one inside that will not open, is handed back whole as an attachment carrying its sentence (Attachment.parks) and parks as a container of its own; an embedded .msg message past the depth has no bytes to hand back and stops the whole container. An unnamed part is 'attachment N' plus the extension its Content-Type names, from a fixed table (mimetypes reads the Windows registry, so two machines would name one part two ways). The CLI lists what a container holds and writes nothing. Decision 178: a zip holding any member packed other than content_check.PACKINGS parks from its directory as CONTAINER_LIMIT (LIMIT_PACKING) before a byte is unpacked; WinZip's AES stays CONTAINER_LOCKED. Decision 176: safe_name() drops every Unicode format character, so a right-to-left override cannot dress a program as a PDF in the firm's review folder. Decision 188: safe_name strips the layout's one invisible set (layout.is_invisible) instead of category Cf alone, keeping white space and control characters for the illegal-character rule; the module no longer imports unicodedata.
- **`tracker/content_check.py`** — Tier 3: extract text (pdfplumber / openpyxl / plain text, OCR for a scan or a photo) and test it against the row's keyword and date rules. extract() is the one reading of a document, used by the router and the scanner alike; ContentCache keeps the verdicts - in the store, per engagement, since decision 107.
  - CLI: `python -m tracker.content_check`
  - constants: `RETIRED_CACHE_FILENAME` = '_content_cache.json', `CACHE_VERSION` = 12, `PAGE_BREAK` = '\x0c', `MAX_PAGES` = 10, `XLSX_EXTENSIONS` = ('xlsx', 'xlsm'), `TEXT_EXTENSIONS` = ('csv', 'tsv', 'txt'), `PIXEL_BUDGET` = 40000000, `RENDER_SCALE` = 2.0, `READING_STOP_PAGE_SECONDS` = 60.0, `READING_STOP_DOCUMENT_SECONDS` = 600.0, `UNKNOWN_PACKING` = "a part of it is packed in a way only a person's zip program opens", `TITLE_CHARS` = 400, `MULTI_FORM_FAMILIES` = 2, `BROKER_FORM` = '1099b', `DATE_LINE_MAX` = 500, `READ_IN_A_CHILD` = True, `OPEN_TEST_FINGERPRINT` = 'open-test'
  - imports: `tracker/__init__.py`, `tracker/ledger.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/ocr.py`, `tracker/reasons.py`, `tracker/records.py`, `tracker/store.py`, `tracker/validators.py`
  - used by: `tools/backtest.py`, `tools/learned_keywords.py`, `tools/vocab_report.py`, `tracker/api.py`, `tracker/containers.py`, `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/names.py`, `tracker/router.py`, `tracker/runner.py`, `tracker/scanner.py`
  - imports at call time: `tracker/door.py`, `tracker/names.py`, `tracker/page.py`
  - writes: `artifact:tracker.db`
  - reads: `artifact:tracker.db`
  - enforces: `rule:no-AI-on-client-documents`
  - tested by: `tests/test_content_check.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/child_readers.py`, `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/test_api.py`, `tests/test_backtest.py`, `tests/test_build.py`, `tests/test_catalog.py`, `tests/test_containers.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_names.py`, `tests/test_ocr.py`, `tests/test_real_corpus.py`, `tests/test_records.py`, `tests/test_review.py`, `tests/test_router.py`, `tests/test_runner.py`, `tests/test_scanner.py`, `tests/test_single_source.py`, `tests/test_store.py`, `tests/test_templates.py`, `tests/test_vocab_report.py`
  - note: The cache stores verdicts only - pass/fail, the reason, and the Evidence behind them, all of it the firm's own words. Extracted client text is never persisted. Only the first MAX_PAGES pages of a PDF are read, text or OCR - the identifying words are up front and a long ledger used to stall a run. Verdicts are keyed by the file's content digest and the row's rules fingerprint (CACHE_VERSION, carried on every row; a row at another version is ignored and dropped), with a per-path memo of size/mtime/digest so an unchanged file is not re-hashed: the same bytes are read twice in this system, once as a drop the router routes and once as the working copy the scanner checks, and a verdict the router reached is the verdict the scanner finds. extract(ocr=False) hands a scan back with needs_ocr set so the router can try the file's name first; extract_by_ocr() finishes the reading. The CLI (python -m tracker.content_check <engagement> <file>) prints what the document says and which rows accept it, writing no cache. DECISION 107 - THE CACHE LEFT THE SYNCED FOLDER: ContentCache(engagement_dir) loads the engagement's memos and verdicts from the store's two tables (store.cached_verdicts()) once, works in memory as it always did, and save() writes what it learned and forgot through store.remember_verdicts() - one immediate transaction of the store's own, under the engagement lock, never store.record(), because a verdict is a derivation of the bytes and the rules and not an event; a pass killed mid-save leaves the previous rows. ContentCache() with no engagement is memory only (the CLI's, a test's) and its save() touches nothing. The engagement must already be in the store or the constructor refuses by name. The JSON cache file that used to sit in the engagement folder is never read; RETIRED_CACHE_FILENAME survives only for the filer's tidy-up, which removes it. THE STEP-0 RE-RUN'S FINDING: decision 105 had kept a two-form split's second verdict in the cache alone, so a rebuilt store read the second copy the ordinary way and failed it - the cache was carrying a decision, not a derivation. own_forms(text) is now the one reading of which forms a page counts as its own (the set of self-named forms when MULTI_FORM_FAMILIES or more families print their own name, else None; the constant moved here from the router, which re-exports it for one release); _check_uncached() reads through it, so the scan's miss verdict is the router's kept verdict for every page, split included, and a delete-and-rebuild leaves every status byte-identical. _evidence_from_json() takes a tuple as well as a list, so a verdict read back in the pass that kept it carries its evidence. Decision 55: contains_keyword() treats a hyphen-joined form variant as part of the form's name (1098 never matches 1098-T); a verdict that is the machine's (no OCR, OCR failed) is transient and never cached. Decision 57: FORM_VARIANTS is the one list of each form's real variants; _JOINER is what may sit between a number and its variant or a keyword's words; the text-layer floor is per page; CACHE_VERSION 3. Decision 60: _seams() lets a keyword typed w2 find W-2; no letters or digits means no keyword. Decision 62: says() is contains_keyword() as content evidence - a form number counts only within TITLE_CHARS; _seams() reads plurals, keeps numbers out of amounts, takes any apostrophe. Decision 63: dominant_forms() - a form number counts in the text when it is in the title or is the number the document mentions most; form <anything> is a form number. Decision 64: dominant_forms() weighs a mention by its shape - a form names itself with its year or revision and another form in a sentence. Decision 66: the title is weighed the same way (_title_forms(); _REFERENCE_BEFORE marks a form quoted after attach/forms/see/of/on/and/or), a number outside FORM_VARIANTS is a mention only after Form, a keyword's words sit on one line or wrap as a heading from a line's start (_WRAPPING_JOINER, _LINE_START), a sheet's cells are tab-separated within a row; CACHE_VERSION 5. Decision 67: what comes before a form is read before what follows it (attach Form 1098 (2025) is a reference); a title naming _LIST_OF_FORMS or more forms names none; the title window is measured on the lower-cased text; _LINE_START admits a bullet, a pipe or a rule. Decision 68: _LIST_OF_FORMS counts families (_FAMILY), so a consolidated 1099 is one family's document; _REFERENCE_BEFORE stays on one line. Decision 69: a form number set off by a dash is a reference (_REFERENCE_AFTER), a dash before the year is still dated (_SELF_AFTER), and _REFERENCE_BEFORE reads across a line break again. Decision 73: says() weighs where a plain keyword is said, not only that it is there - an occurrence that is a menu line's title (_menu_tails: a form number and the title a dash or a comma sets off from it are one reference) or what an ask-word asked for (_asked_for: attach, provide, send, see and their kin, governing the rest of their own sentence and the line a request wraps on to) is the page talking about a document rather than being one, and one occurrence that is neither is enough. A dash-set-off form that heads its line with a year beside it, where the title window holds no second such line and no ask precedes it, names itself (_titles_its_own_line), so a payer's substitute form is not read as a checklist. A form number after a comma continues a list (_LIST_CONTINUES), and enclosed/enclosure/enclosures/re: join _REFERENCE_BEFORE, which now reads a colon between the word and the form. any_keyword_matched() answers the router's question 'did this row's keywords match, apart from the year?'. CACHE_VERSION 6. Decision 82: a verdict keeps the evidence behind it. Evidence(rule, term, where, page) is the one shape - EVIDENCE_RULES (required, any, date, filename, refused) and EVIDENCE_PLACES (title, first_page, footer, deep) are the named values, imported by the router, the index and the app's vocabulary and retyped nowhere. The Evidence record, those two lists and the cell format that format_evidence() writes and parse_evidence() reads now live in tracker/records.py (decision 100) and are re-exported here for one release; what stays here is the reading of a document that produces them. says() became a thin wrapper over _says_where(), which reaches the same verdict by the same reading and also says where the word was found (_where_said(): the title window first, then a page's last _FOOTER_LINES non-blank lines, then the rest of page 1, then deep), so no placement moved. evaluate_rules() puts an Evidence per matched rule on ContentResult.evidence, on a failing verdict too, and the reason sentence is untouched; the date rule records the row's Period, not the regex it derives and not a word of the document. format_evidence()/parse_evidence() are the one owner of the index cell's compact form (term@where:page rule, candidates joined by '; '), and the page is left off when it is 0. CACHE_VERSION 7, because a version-6 verdict read back would claim a verdict with no reason behind it. Decision 85: a form heading its own line with its printed title after its number and its year after the title names itself, at the weight a bare number-then-year mention carries - _names_itself() is the one predicate, and it holds both shapes a printed title wears (a dash between number and title, decision 69/73's; or nothing between them, _SELF_TITLED). The IRS's 2024 and 2025 W-2 revisions print one copy to the page, so Copy B's only "W-2" is the foot's "W-2 Wage and Tax Statement 2025 Department of the Treasury" and the form said nothing about itself before this. The year must be a year and not a date's tail ("Form 941 04/30/2025" on a CP 575 is a filing deadline), and a page heading two such lines is a menu, as it is for the dashed shape - _lists_forms() counts both. CACHE_VERSION 8, because a cached verdict from before it would say a one-copy W-2 is nobody's form. Decision 90: a keyword may name alternatives and join the phrases one of them wants together, read through manifest.keyword_alternatives() - says() takes the first alternative whose every phrase is said and places the evidence at its leading phrase, contains_keyword() reads a file name the same way, and a keyword holding neither character is one phrase exactly as before. CACHE_VERSION 9, because a verdict cached before it read the '|' and the '+' as words to look for. Decision 109: ContentCache.digest_of() is now the one memo for every hash of a file under Prepared/ - the filer's sweep and its proof of each copy it makes, a person's filing as the scan reads it, and the scan's own de-duplication - so a second and a third pass over an unchanged tree cost stats rather than reads. Nothing under the tree a client is shared is ever memo'd: decision 68 reads every preserved original each pass by design, and that is the one reading the measure allows. The scan's prune() now keeps every file under Prepared/, so a parked copy's memo and a stray's survive the pass that learned them. DECISION 127 - PHOTOS, AND THE PAGE UPRIGHT: extract_text() returns None for an IMAGE_EXTENSIONS file on purpose (an image never has a text layer) and extract() reads that as 'this is a scan' rather than 'no extractor', so a photo takes the scanned-PDF path exactly - needs_ocr with ocr=False, extract_by_ocr() otherwise, which dispatches _ocr_pdf for a PDF and _ocr_image for a photo. _ocr_image() undoes the phone's EXIF rotation first (ImageOps.exif_transpose), then reads. (Decision 127 turned every page upright with Tesseract's OSD and a four-way score; decision 169 removed both with Tesseract - see below.) The file on disk is never touched, because a photo is an original. CACHE_VERSION 10, because a verdict reached at 9 may have been reached on a page nobody turned. Extraction.seconds carries how long each reading took (extract() times _extract() and stamps it), which decides nothing - no reading is capped, timed out or abandoned; the router carries it into the pass. reasons.NO_TEXT_LAYER now says 'PDF or photo'. Decision 137: extract() never opens a file past validators.MAX_READ_MB (reasons.TOO_LARGE, a kept verdict); a .csv/.tsv/.txt is read to validators.TEXT_READ_CAP_MB and Extraction.cut says so, and a failing verdict on a cut text ends with reasons.TEXT_CUT. OCR renders each PDF page at render_scale() - min(RENDER_SCALE, sqrt(PIXEL_BUDGET / page area)) - so no page passes 40 Mpx, and a photo is held to the same budget before decoding (JPEG draft, else reduced on decode; Pillow's guard stays on). A Date Pattern is compiled and run line by line (date_pattern_at), lines over DATE_LINE_MAX skipped, bounding a backtracking typo. A picture past Pillow's own decompression-bomb limit raises TooLargeToRead and is a kept reasons.TOO_LARGE verdict, not a retry. Decision 137 Part B (B1.2): the safety stop - READING_STOP_PAGE_SECONDS (60) and READING_STOP_DOCUMENT_SECONDS (600), a photo one page - is a _SafetyStop set for each extract_by_ocr() reading; since decision 169 (ruling 5) no page starts past it (_SafetyStop.page() checks before each page), a PDF page's render counts against it, and ReadingStopped becomes a kept reasons.READING_STOPPED verdict, not retried until the file changes. _clock is named so the suite moves it. Review fix (F7): a Period-derived date pattern runs over the whole text as before; only a staff pattern runs line by line. Part B review fixes: the stop's sentence says '1 minute'; extract()'s docstring states what the stop covers in-process (between pages) and what only the child's end covers (a page being read, the text layer, one render). DECISION 150 - A READING RUNS WHERE IT CAN BE STOPPED: extract_bounded() is what the pass reads through (router.read_once and _check_uncached); it runs open_and_read() - validators.open_test() (tier 2's open test) then extract() - in a spawned child (_read_in_a_child, the child itself in tracker/ocr.py since decision 169, over multiprocessing's Pipe: a named pipe on Windows, never a socket) and waits at most reading_stop_seconds() - READING_STOP_DOCUMENT_SECONDS for a file, READING_STOP_PAGE_SECONDS for a photo. On time the child's Extraction is returned as is; over time _end() ends the child's whole tree (taskkill /T on Windows, the child's own process group elsewhere) and the reading is abandoned() - the same kept READING_STOPPED verdict B1.2 gives; a child that ends without answering, or whose reader raised, is reading_failed() - reasons.READING_CRASHED, firm-side, kept. B1.2 stays inside the child. The child writes nothing; since decision 169 neither does the reader (no temporary file), so ocr_scratch is gone. READ_IN_A_CHILD is True in the tracker and turned off for the suite by tests/conftest.py (its fakes live in the test's process); _CHILD_READER is what the child runs, open_and_read() by default, so tests/child_readers.py can hand the child a reader that blocks or dies. A cached verdict never starts a child; the benchmark and the CLI call extract() directly. The child never outlives its pass (the designer's ruling on the build): its lifeline and its job object moved with it to tracker/ocr.py in decision 169, which says how. The review's ruling: the open test's verdict rides back as Extraction.opened; the router hands it to every row's check_file(open_test=...) and keeps it under OPEN_TEST_FINGERPRINT by digest; the scanner's check_files asks open_verdict(), which answers from that kept verdict or reads the file in a child and holds the reading in memory (ContentCache.hold_reading, never saved) for the content check that follows; HEIC_NOT_SUPPORTED is the machine's and not kept. The child says 'started' before it touches the file: no word before the stop, an end before it, or a Process that cannot start is could_not_start() - reasons.READER_UNAVAILABLE, transient, nothing kept - and readers_that_could_not_start() is what the runner's pass (and the app's Run now) turns into one warning. Decision 141: FIRST_PAGE_PHRASES (a notice's header phrases - notice date, tax year, tax period, irs, internal revenue service) count only when first said on page 1, so a bill whose back page talks about a notice is not one; only the catalog's notices row uses them. CACHE_VERSION 11. Decision 154: in_a_child(path, job, stop=..., **kwargs) is the one child mechanism, and _read_in_a_child() is the reading's use of it; it gives (answer, None) on time or (None, the Extraction that says why - abandoned(), reading_failed() or could_not_start()), so the opening of an email or a zip (containers.open_bounded) runs in the same child, under the same stop, lifeline and job object. Since decision 169 it hands the job to tracker.ocr.run_in_child() - the pass's one long-lived child - and words the ocr.Outcome it gets back; it no longer makes a process of its own. Decision 155 added ContentCache.remember_digest(): a digest proved on a working copy's temp is remembered for the copy's name after the rename (same size, same modification time), so the proof is still one read. DECISION 169 - RAPIDOCR IS THE READER: _ocr_pdf() renders each page at render_scale() and hands it, in RGB, to ocr.read_page(); _ocr_image() hands the EXIF-upright photo the same way. Nothing turns a page (ruling 6 as re-ruled: RapidOCR keeps a sideways page's words; the turning rule arrives in ocr._upright_lines() as the amendment '169, upright'). ocr.ReaderUnavailable - a model missing or broken - is None from the reader, so reasons.NO_TEXT_LAYER, transient, now worded 'the reader could not run on this machine'. The pages are still joined with a line break, never PAGE_BREAK (SPEC-127.2X D9.2). pytesseract, _tesseract, _upright, _four_way, _score_of, _for_scoring and their constants are gone, and ocr_scratch with them (the reader writes no temporary file - SPEC-169 section 6). CACHE_VERSION 12: every verdict on a scan or a photo was the old reader's. Decision 178: a reading is bounded in what it hands back, whatever it reads. READING_CHAR_BUDGET (TEXT_READ_CAP_MB counted in characters) bounds every reading - the workbook and PDF readers stop at it, _extract cuts past it and marks the reading cut. PACKINGS (stored, deflated) is the only zip packing a reading unpacks: a workbook packed otherwise fails with UNKNOWN_PACKING, and containers refuses such a zip. _line_of finds a line's ends by the nearest break of any kind - forward by one search, back over a window that doubles until it meets a break, and a mention on the line last found reuses it - linear where it was quadratic. Decision 189 (SPEC-161 A-F9): _clock, the child's _SafetyStop clock, is ocr.awake_clock, so time the machine slept is never counted against a reading. Decision 189 (the judgment worker): the reader child judges as well as reads. judge(path, questions) makes the open test and the reading, then answers every question the pass asks: each row's verdict (evaluate_rules with own_forms, which is also decision 94's split), both router leads (required_matched, any_keyword_matched), self_named_forms, own_forms, carries_a_1099b_section, and the name check (names.check_name, reached at call time). It hands back a Judgment that carries no word of the document. The pass calls judge_bounded (in the child, or in-process when READ_IN_A_CHILD is off). judgment_of is the pure judgment for callers that already hold an Extraction (the backtest, via route_file(reading=...)). The answers are the pre-189 values call for call, so CACHE_VERSION did not move (claim 3.g). Rows are keyed by RowQuestion (the five rule fields), not the rules fingerprint, which omits period and date_pattern_derived; the cache still keys by fingerprint. dominant_forms and self_named_forms run once per judgment. OCR text is cut to READING_CHAR_BUDGET. ContentCache holds Judgments, not texts. Decision 76: dismiss_review_file() rewrites a parked row NOT_REQUESTED with the DISMISSED_BY_PERSON reason and moves nothing; _find_parked() takes a dismissed row too, so filing it is the undo. Decision 111: a re-send is judged by the earlier row's decision - the content hash says which row holds those bytes and that row's decision says what this drop is. It never overwrites (a file already at home that is not this document stays exactly where it is; this document's copy goes to review under the client's own name and the row parks naming both, PUT_BACK_REFUSED), never deletes (a home that already holds these bytes leaves the wanderer where it is for a person to remove, PUT_BACK_ALREADY) and never guesses (the row's sequence number first, every byte it is about to move second, the move third, and a refused record puts back exactly what moved). Every location the row claims is put back, not the Prepared Location column alone: the sweep names the first location that failed, and a page decision 94 filed under several requests has a copy in each, each remade from the one just put back. One event whatever the click found, ledger.RESTORED_BY_PERSON, because the row it carries says which. The other two answers are the actions that already existed: keep-it-here is assign_review_file() on a moved row, where the copy that moves is the wanderer and the request may be the folder's own or another the person picks; send-it-to-review is unfile_document(), where the wanderer is the copy that goes back and a row whose bytes are nowhere is copied from the original. Both refuse a row with copies under several requests by name (SEVERAL_COPIES_REFUSAL) and point at put-it-back. find_parked() and find_filed() take accepting=, the decisions the action will have beyond the ones they were written for, so those two reach a FILE_MOVED row and dismiss_review_file() still refuses one by name (decision 76); find_moved() is their shape over FILE_MOVED itself. DECISION 119 - AN INTERRUPTED MOVE IS FINISHED FROM THE RECORD, NEVER GUESSED: before the first file operation of any decision - a pass's copy, a person's filing, unfiling or put-back - _intend() appends ledger.MOVING under the lock, keyed by the row's own ledger key, carrying the operations in order with the digest each end should hold, the row the decision will record, the event that will complete it, who decided and (for a drop's own move, which has no row yet) the day the run began; _do_op() is the one place a plan is carried out, by the decision and by the recovery alike, so a move a recovery makes is the move the decision would have made. _finish_interrupted_moves() runs at the start of every pass, under the lock, after the index is read and before the digests of rows recorded without them are filled in, before the client's folder is read for strays and before the sweep - so a person's half-made filing is finished and recorded as theirs rather than swept up as a copy somebody dragged. Each operation is checked by bytes and finished where reality matches; the intent's row is then recorded as the intent said, with the events that travelled with it, dated the day the person decided. Where a destination holds other bytes nothing there is touched and the row parks with reasons.INTERRUPTED_MOVE naming it (interrupted_at() and interrupted_note() read the sentence back for the scanner, as moved_to() does 109's); where neither end holds the bytes the row parks with INTERRUPTED_MOVE_LOST; either way the copy a person acts on is the one waiting in review if there is one, else a fresh one from the client's original. _refuse_if_a_move_is_open() refuses all four person actions while an intent is open here, before 112's freshness check, because the next pass - or Run now - finishes it. A refused record rolls back as it always did and appends ledger.MOVE_ABANDONED so the next pass does not finish forward a move the record would not take. RECORD_PRESERVE_INTENTS is the one switch: the pass's own move into the client's folder is already finished by decision 23, and its intent buys only the received date. _plan_working_copy() took over from the filer's old one-step copy helper: deciding where a working copy goes and making it are two steps now, because what will happen has to be written down before it does. refuse_a_path_past_the_limit() lives here since decision 126: the deepest thing a return ever holds is a working copy this module writes, and both creation (tracker.api) and the household rollover (tracker.rollover, at a layer below the API) measure it before a folder is made. The name tier (decision 128) runs inside file_household_drops: one reading per drop, then check_name() per accepting return against that return's own people. A named request keeps its acceptance only where the name confirms, an unnamed one keeps it where the name is merely absent, and any return whose page names somebody on another return of the household is dropped. What is left goes to the exactly-one rule; a list the name emptied parks in the home return with reasons.NAME_NOT_ON_PAGE, NAMES_ANOTHER_RETURN or NO_PEOPLE_ON_FILE, in that order. A filing by hand may teach one spelling, recorded as one rules_changed event inside the filing's own transaction exactly as a taught keyword is. A list the name emptied parks in the first return that ACCEPTED the document (decision 125's home), the first return by folder order only where nothing accepted it at all. Both of decision 111's re-send roads - a row a person set aside, a filed row whose working copy is gone - are name-checked the same way inside _sort_one() before they file, or the check could be walked round by sending a document twice. Decision 129 widened the sort from the household's own returns to its feed list, and decision 132 re-specified it: file_household_drops(inbox, originals, own=, fed=) takes the two lists by name, judges own returns first (the bytes are asked of the records in that order - the record closest to the drop decides - while the locks were taken in the global one), a document nobody may file always parks in a home return (_the_home), and every filing goes through _file_into() - ONE SHAPE FOR THE PASS AND A PERSON: one intent in the TARGET's record, keyed on the row's final location, ops [move original -> resting] (only where the household differs, which since decision 204 is only a person's hand-over) + [copy resting -> each working copy], then the row (FILED for the pass, ASSIGNED_BY_PERSON for a person) and its also events; nothing ever writes into another return's record. DECISION 204 (revising 132): THE PASS NEVER FILES ACROSS HOUSEHOLDS, on a first arrival or a re-send (_decide_across and _sort_one alike). A document only a return in another household is left with parks at home: OPENED_NOT_ACROSS (an attachment), UNNAMED_ACROSS_HOUSEHOLDS (names nobody; the picker), or NAMED_ACROSS_HOUSEHOLDS (names that return's person; _NameStage.spelling keeps the firm's matched spelling for the reason, _named_across) with the row's waits_for cell (_waits_for: records.format_waits_for of the return's household and name, routing.filed_to and the Also Answers, each filtered to that list as _file_it filters them). _ReturnRun.dropped_in, _rests_at's second move and runner.FILED_INTO_FED are gone; _file_it's original rests where the inbox move left it. hand_over(also=, answers=, waiting=) is the only road across: requests_taking() is the one list-and-N/A check (the API's card offer uses it too), one copy per request (decision 94) and the filtered answers cell (146) on the taking row, waits_for cleared; waiting=True is the one click - under both locks, after the seq check, _refuse_unless_it_waits_for() refuses (NOT_WAITING or a claim mismatch) unless the row is still NEEDS_REVIEW with NAMED_ACROSS_HOUSEHOLDS and its claim names the target by waiting_target() (layout.name_key on household and return, decision 188) and exactly these requests and answers. hand_over() is two intents in two records, each finished by its own household's pass with no lock it does not hold: the home's release intent first (remove the parked copy, then ledger.RELEASED with RELEASED_TO as its reason - the row leaves the index, the dropping household keeps no row), then the taking return's filing through _file_into(), its row, the home's remove and the release. A kill after the release intent alone costs the person's click (the original, named by no row, is a stray re-sorted where it lies). A PASS LEAVES ALONE AN ORIGINAL ANOTHER RECORD'S OPEN INTENT NAMES (the lead's ruling R-1): _named_by_another_records_intent() - asked only when a stray is found - reads every return of the practice (positionally, each followed to its journal first, no lock) for an open intent naming that path with those bytes as a step's source, and such a file is never re-sorted, parked or recorded - but it is said, LEFT_FOR_ANOTHER_RETURN on the first own return's attention every pass it happens (ruling R-3), so an intent that never finishes never leaves an original unmentioned; so the taking return's recovery always finishes the move and each half of a hand-over is finished by its own household's pass. _decide_across() records a reading's seconds on first (the first own return, the run the inbox's own notes ride - SPEC-127.1 9.2). Decision 127: FileReport.slowest holds the run's SLOWEST_READINGS longest readings as (name, seconds), recorded by FileReport.timed() off Routing.seconds after each drop is routed - after the fact, so nothing is ever cut short for being slow. Decision 131: THE ROOM A RETURN HAS - room_for(engagement_dir, items) -> Room(need, least, floor, parks, short, limit), from the list alone (no disk, no store, no lock): need is creation's figure (refuse_a_path_past_the_limit is now need > MAX_PATH_LENGTH), least the deepest path at shortest_name_for() (identifier, period, ' (99)', extension), floor the review folder plus 'x (99).<ext>', parks the rows whose shortest name passes their extension's limit, short how far the deepest canonical copy passes the limit for ITS extension (layout.limit_for). prepared_name_for(..., room=) CUTS THE DOCUMENT PART to fit the room the exact destination folder leaves - identifier, period, numbered suffix and extension never cut, the suffix counted in the same loop - and raises NoRoom (a FilingError whose sentence is PATH_NO_ROOM) when not even the shortest form fits; room=None is the canonical name exactly. _plan_working_copy, a person's filing and hand_over pass a room; the pass parks a NoRoom document with PATH_NO_ROOM (the last reason the filing branch gives; the request that accepted it is its candidate), a person is refused with it and nothing moves. _unique_path(..., room=) cuts a review copy's stem the same way (_review_copy_path: a reader's limit never stops a park - it falls back to Windows's, which the pass's floor has proved); original_name stays the client's whole name; an original is never cut. The sentences HOUSEHOLD_NO_ROOM, ROOM_SHORT and ROOM_PARKS live here beside PATH_NO_ROOM. THE REVIEW'S FIXES: every sentence names the limit as that kind of copy's ('the 218 characters a .xlsx copy may have'), never 'Windows allows'; PATH_NO_ROOM_IN names a fed return by label when its request has no room and the document parks at home; EVERY review copy - _park_it, the recovery's _a_copy_to_act_on, unfile_document, restore_working_copy's refused put-back - is named through _review_copy_path(review_dir, name) -> (path, note), whose note is REVIEW_COPY_PAST_READER when a workbook's copy was fitted to 260 past a reader's 218; _unique_path(room=) cuts a name whose suffix is not an extension as one stem, and below one character raises NoRoom with REVIEW_NO_ROOM (never a request's label); _a_copy_to_act_on returns (location, sentence) and a copy it cannot make leaves the row naming NO copy; _plan_working_copy and assign_review_file find an existing copy by its bytes BEFORE measuring a name; no request folder is made until every copy of a filing is named (_do_op makes the parent); _stem_of's cap cuts the label, never the period. Decision 137 (L2): _move_whole() takes the folder its walk started from (within=) and asks the link question again of every folder from the source up to it immediately before os.rename; a link anywhere raises MovedThroughALinkError (an OSError, so every caller already says "left in place"). Decision 137 Part B (M2): _decide_across() filed into a return in another household (_across_households, against the dropping household's own first run) only when the name tier CONFIRMED the page (decision 204 closed that road too: a confirmed page parks with NAMED_ACROSS_HOUSEHOLDS); a document kept only because its request is unnamed parks at home with reasons.UNNAMED_ACROSS_HOUSEHOLDS. Within one household decision 128's table is unchanged, and a person's own filing across (File it) is untouched. Review fix (F5): the link check (door.through_a_link since decision 188) judges only the folders between its root and the path, and refuses a path that is not under the root. Part B review fixes: _across_households() reads run.home (the dropping household's own), never a fallback run; a B2 park's Evidence names the return and request that wanted it (_with_the_wanting_return, keyed '<label> / <identifier>'); _sort_one() returns the run its row goes into, and an unnamed re-send a return in another household already holds parks at home with the same sentence. Decision 150 (the designer's ruling on the re-review): _not_read(reading) - a reader that could not start (reasons.READER_UNAVAILABLE, transient) - makes _decide_across() and _sort_one() return None, and _sort_all() records nothing for that drop: no index row, no Needs Review row, nothing kept. A drop already moved rests in the year's folder with no row, so the next pass reads it again as a stray (the shape of unfinished_drops); the pass's one READER_COULD_NOT_START warning is its only trace. A machine's fault leaves nothing permanent. Decision 143: _sort_all() opens an email or a zip after its move and fingerprint and before the decision (_open_container): the container is recorded OPENED in the first own return, its journal line (ledger.OPENED) carrying each attachment and each part skipped (the run's opened map, merged into the event by _rows_changed's extra); each attachment is written atomically under layout.opened_dir_of() by _take_out() (reused by bytes after a kill, numbered past other bytes, cut to fit) before the container's row exists, then decided by _decide_attachment() through _decide_across() with _SortContext.container set so every row it writes, and the intent before it, names the container. The first own return is recorded last, so a kill between two returns' transactions leaves the container a stray to reopen. An attachment never files into, or writes a row in, another household (_decide_across parks it at home with reasons.OPENED_NOT_ACROSS, and asks only the returns _may_hold() allows whether they hold its bytes, so no Duplicate row reaches another household's record - the review's B1; hand_over refuses it). replaced_in_pbc() is asked of _Opened as well as the year's folder (the review's B2). _unaccounted_in_opened() says every pass what sits under _Opened that no row names. FileReport.opened lists the containers; DUPLICATE_OF_OPENED is a re-sent one. Decision 150 over 143 (the restack): an attachment is read through _decide_across and so in 150's child; one whose reader could not start gets no row (_decide_attachment returns False), and then neither does its container - its opened entry is withdrawn and its folder put in _ReturnRun.reopen, so _unaccounted_in_opened says nothing of it - and the next pass reopens the container as a stray, reuses each file by its bytes, skips each attachment a row names and reads the one that waited. Decision 144: _parts_of() reads RequestItem.short_name, so prepared_name_for() and shortest_name_for() name a copy <identifier> - <short> - <period>, 131's cut cuts the short name first, and room_for() measures the short names - under the firm's own 35-character root none of the owner's 39 intake returns is refused. Decision 155: _copy_whole() is fsio.copy_atomically() with the digest proved on the temp before the swap (CopyMismatchError, decision 17's could-not-be-filed row), and the proved digest handed to ContentCache.remember_digest() so the proof still costs one read; a killed or failed copy leaves only its temp, never a file under the working copy's name, and the copy is writable. sweep_stranded_temps(household, returns, started) is called by runner.run_household under every return's lock before anything is read: it removes the tracker's own temps (fsio.TEMP_NAME's exact shape, born before the pass, left by this process or one locking.pid_alive() says is gone) under each return's folder, under the household-year's _Opened and beside the README in the inbox under the README's lock, never a path any row of these returns names (a parked copy keeps the client's name, an attachment its own) and never through a link (fsio.is_link, which replaced the filer's own _is_link and _LINK_TAGS) - never in a client year folder, never a client's .tmp - and never raises. UNRECORDED_COPY's advice no longer assumes a client's document (audit E8) and never sends one to a client's folder (decision 184): confirm whose it is, then the app or a firm-side folder a person controls; anything else is deleted by hand. Decision 160: received_for() joins a filed row to its request without case (identifier_key) and labels it in the list's spelling, so a respelling by case reads received in the README as in the letter. documents_by_request() counts Filed and File Moved rows per request from the index. rename_request() gives a request another identifier in one act in decision 119's shape: checks under the lock (open intents, the list's version, the list's validation, every copy there with its bytes, no destination taken, path length), then one store.record of the renaming events and one MOVING intent per changed row (then renamed_by_person), then the moves, then the rows; a failed move after the write is finished forward by the next pass (RENAME_UNFINISHED). Case-only, File Moved copies and taken destinations are refused. DECISION 168: every copy is written to Prepared/<name> - the request-folder lookup is gone, prepared_location() says Prepared/<name> for a copy in Prepared itself - and copies_of() narrows _existing_copy() to one request's own copies, so decision 94's page is never reused across requests; room_for() measures Prepared/<name>; _request_of_copy() reads an also-filed copy's request from its own name; the sweep says an unrecorded file named for a request or in the review folder, and a person's folder is the scanner's to name, once. The rename moves copies only, in place, and there is no emptied request folder to remove; an intent written before 168 names folder-shaped paths and is finished as written. A working copy's number takes Prepared's own names, and the Prepared names an open intent will write to (decision 147's context.intended), as taken. Decision 147: iter_drops() returns the inbox in its own order (_inbox_order: the top level first, then each subfolder in case-folded name order, a folder's own files before its subfolders'), so of two files of one name the top-level one keeps it; a drop from a subfolder carries CAME_FROM_SUBFOLDER (the path below the inbox, backslashed) at the end of whichever row it gets, through _SortContext.came_from, set around the drop's decision like container and cleared around each attachment's (the inbox move writes no intent, so a kill between the move and the row loses the sentence - the accepted limit). _unique_path() is the one numbering function - the inbox move, hand_over(), review copies and _take_out() all call it (the pass's second move, _rests_at, went with decision 204) - and a name is taken when the disk holds it or a row of the household-year names it (_on_record(), the union unrecorded_in_pbc() reads against; _year_on_record() reads every return of the household-year, the pass's in hand and any return the pass left out (an inactive one; the review's N-1) from its record - the inbox move and _take_out through _taken_in_the_year() and hand_over() directly), or an open intent of the pass will write to it (_SortContext.intended, from _spoken_for_by_an_open_intent(ends=TO), joined by _taken_names()), unless the incoming bytes are that row's own (audit F-1): a different document never lands on a name a deleted original left, so it never becomes that row's next version. DECISION 157 - A MISSING WORKING COPY IS MADE AGAIN, NEVER ASKED FOR AGAIN: the sweep (_prove_working_copies) no longer skips a row whose copy is gone with its bytes nowhere (what was 'decision 3's regression'). For a Filed or parked row, and a File Moved row that already says nowhere whose every claimed place is simply gone (_may_be_made_again), each absent place is made again from the row's original, read in the moment and proved against the row's digest (_the_original_now: proved; unread - a placeholder or a read refused, and nothing is written; gone - absent or other bytes), through _make_again - an intent (then=ledger.COPY_REMADE) and decision 155's whole copy, all or nothing (_take_back and _abandon on a failure, REMAKE_FAILED said) - the row gaining REMADE_SENTENCE (a File Moved row goes back to Filed or Needs Review, _remade) and the pass one attention line; the request's status does not move. Where the original is gone too the row is FILE_MOVED with BOTH_GONE_SENTENCE, said once (both_gone() reads it, behind any person's marks; _moved_part splits a Reason round its moved sentence). A File Moved row whose wanderer vanishes is said nowhere first (MOVED_GONE_SENTENCE, or BOTH_GONE_SENTENCE where the original is absent) and is made again the pass after. Mark missing (mark_missing_again) accepts a row's own identifier on a both_gone() row only: the row keeps its decision and gains MARKED_MISSING, its prepared_location, also_filed and answers come off (marked_missing() is that shape), one answer_withdrawn_by_person line; such a row claims nothing, is left out of _missing_positions (no MISSING_IN_PBC, never followed), received_for and documents_by_request (_counts_as_received), and a re-send of its bytes - or of a both_gone() row's - is re-filed (REFILED_AFTER_GONE). restore_working_copy() dispatches: a FILE_MOVED row to _put_back_a_moved_copy (decision 110, unchanged, but a nowhere row whose original is gone refuses with NOTHING_TO_PUT_BACK), a Filed or parked row with a gone copy (_find_to_put_back, _gone_copies) to _make_a_gone_copy_again - the pass's _make_again, REMADE_SENTENCE and COPY_REMADE, decided by the person; a marked row refuses (MARKED_REFUSAL); keep-it-here and send-to-review refuse a both-gone row with NOTHING_TO_PUT_BACK, and send-to-review proves the original before it writes its intent. A RETURNING ORIGINAL (ruling B7, audit C5, 147's N-4): _sort_all asks _originals_away() (rows whose recorded original is absent, by digest - not an attachment, a marked row or a place an open intent will write) and a drop whose bytes are exactly one such row's goes back to that place by _put_back_home() - one intent (the move, plus the copies of a both_gone() row), no new row, ledger.ORIGINAL_RETURNED, RETURNED_SENTENCE put before any moved sentence (_before_the_moved_sentence), and the MISSING_IN_PBC and both-gone lines this pass said taken back (_ReturnRun.absence_said). _unique_path's exception is gone: a name a row names is taken whatever the bytes, so a same-bytes drop _put_back_home does not take is a Duplicate with a key of its own and no row is ever replaced. Decision 179: iter_drops() skips the inbox's README only when scaffold.whose_readme() says it is the firm's; a client's own file of that name is sorted like any drop, and one it cannot tell just now is left where it is and named in the pass's warnings. Decision 180: _may_touch() says where a step of a return may act - under the return, under its household's year _Opened, and in the client tree under some household's inbox or year folder, this return's household where the step writes - and _intend(), _do_op() and _finish_the_ops() refuse any step outside those places (OP_OUTSIDE) before it is recorded or anything moves - reads may come from any year's _Opened of the household, so a cross-year hand-over of an attachment stands - and the recovery's _a_copy_to_act_on() and _the_trouble() hold a row's pbc_location to the same places; locate() stays lexical and never raises. Decision 189 (SPEC-161 ruling 1): _sort_all() saves every return's verdict cache before it takes each file (a no-op when nothing changed), and file_household_drops() saves them again in the finally, after the rows, so neither a kill nor an exception loses a reading already made. Decision 189 (the bounded household, ruling 2.2): file_household_drops(deadline=) hands the deadline to every return's ContentCache for _sort_all(); past it a file whose bytes a return's record holds is still decided from the record (it reads nothing), and the first file that would need a new judgment stops the sort before it is moved - FileReport.unreached (on the first own return's report) counts what waits, unrecorded, for the next pass. A drop on record that must be routed afresh (a re-file, a re-send after a set-aside) stops at the judgment itself (content_check.OutOfTime from _judged() or _sort_one()), after its move: a stray the next pass sorts where it lies; an attachment stopped so waits, its container is left unrecorded and opened again next pass, and the household is out of time as for an unreached drop (_open_container re-raises OutOfTime to _sort_all; the review's M2). Decision 189 (the judgment worker): the household pass asks one judgment per drop. _judged sends every run's rows and one NameQuestion per run (_name_question) through router.read_once. route_file gets judgment=, and the name tier _by_the_name reads judgment.name(...) instead of calling check_name on text. _not_read reads judgment.extraction (the SPEC-156 seam). _sort_one asks its own return's rows and one name question. Decision 187 (first commit): _may_touch() is a one-line call to layout.place_problem(), the rule's one wording, and OP_OUTSIDE names the code in brackets after the location ('for a step (not-a-place)'). Decision 187 (second commit): _refuse_a_step_outside() reads both ends of a step from ledger.op_ends(); _do_op() also runs _refuse_a_step_through_a_link() before any mkdir - a source that is a link, or any folder between the clients root and either end that is one, raises MovedThroughALinkError (MOVE_THROUGH_A_LINK now says 'nothing was moved, copied or removed'), and _a_copy_to_act_on() holds a row's pbc_location to the same link check (A-7). COPY_UNPROVED: _do_op() and _copy_whole() refuse a copy with a blank digest; _intend() fills each blank copy digest in place through _prove() - from the earlier step of the same intent that brings the source in (its digest or its own source's bytes), else from the source's bytes - or raises COPY_UNPROVED before anything is recorded, which the pass's 'could not be filed' branch takes; the three direct _copy_whole() calls pass 'digest or sha256_of(source)'. Decision 187's review: _refuse_a_step_outside passes removes for a removal (M4); _finish_the_ops asks _refuse_a_step_through_a_link of every step before it reads or removes a byte (M3), and fingerprints a blank-digest copy's source itself so an interrupted intent from before 187 finishes (S3); _prove raises COPY_UNREAD, not COPY_UNPROVED, for a source that is there but cannot be read now (S6). Decision 188: the link check moved to door.through_a_link (imported as through_a_link, its only definition); _do_op asks door.client_write (_through_the_door) for a destination in the client tree and every folder made above it before any mkdir; sweep_stranded_temps asks the door before removing a README temp in the inbox; the walks use layout.parts_below instead of relative_to/relpath; the private tree is layout.private_tree_of. The engagement_dir CLI reads its folder through door.return_dir. Review of 188 (S2): _prune_empty_dirs removes an emptied folder in the inbox only through door.client_write.
- **`tracker/fsio.py`** — The one way the tracker writes a file, whole or not at all, and nothing else: TEMP_SUFFIX (what a temp file ends in, and what every walk ignores), TEMP_NAME (the one exact shape of a temp: the target's name, the process id, eight hex digits, .tmp) with temp_owner() reading a name against it, temp_path_for() (a temp name of that shape beside the target), atomic_replacement() (the context manager that writes to the temp, os.replace()s it over the target when the block ends cleanly and fsyncs the folder where the platform allows), write_text_atomically() / write_json_atomically() / write_bytes_atomically() / copy_atomically() over it, each flushing its bytes before the swap, make_writable(), is_link() (the package's one test of a symlink or a junction, from os.lstat's reparse tag, moved down from the filer by decision 155's review), and stranded_temps() (the temps of that shape a killed write left in a folder - it finds, it never removes).
  - constants: `TEMP_SUFFIX` = '.tmp'
  - used by: `tracker/api.py`, `tracker/door.py`, `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/rollover.py`, `tracker/runner.py`, `tracker/scaffold.py`, `tracker/scheduling.py`, `tracker/settings.py`, `tracker/validators.py`, `tracker/view.py`
  - used at call time by: `tracker/store.py`
  - tested by: `tests/test_fsio.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/test_containers.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_scaffold.py`, `tests/test_settings.py`
  - note: Decision 120, and no behaviour change: the five names moved here verbatim from tracker/manifest.py, where they had lived because the manifest was once the workbook they were written for. Layer 0, importing nothing of the package, because every layer writes a file of its own and the one that is lowest must be able to reach the write - which is how there comes to be only one. It holds NO POLICY: nothing here knows what a file is for, which folder it belongs in, whether it may be written or who may write it; the module that owns the file owns every other question about it. The manifest does not re-export them - asking it for one raises at the import (tests/test_manifest.py) - and tracker/settings.py, which borrowed the write and nothing else, came down to layer 0 with them. What did NOT move then: tracker/reminder.py's draft, which decision 155 moved onto write_text_atomically - a torn draft failed its own fingerprint and read as a person's edit for good. Decision 137 (M1) added the one policy-free way a folder is made: make_new_folders() makes every missing level with exist_ok=False and hands back the levels THIS call made, outermost first. That list is the whole of what a failed create or rollover may remove (api._undo_made, rollover._roll_one), so a folder that was already there - a person's own, an old return's - is never removed. Decision 143 added write_bytes_atomically(), flushed before the swap, for an attachment taken out of an email or zip. Decision 155 made it the ONE way every file the tracker writes is written, whole or not there: write_text_atomically() flushes and fsyncs before the swap (NTFS journals the rename, not the data, so settings.json or a README could come back empty after a power cut); copy_atomically() is copy2 into the temp (the bytes and the modification time the verdict memo keys on), make_writable() on the temp - a read-only original's attribute is never carried onto a working copy, whose removal then jammed the household - fsync, then prove(temp) before the swap, so a copy that is not the document never holds the name. The working copy (filer._copy_whole), the reminder draft and the store's export moved onto it. What keeps it honest is the autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py: after every test a store is built from nothing and held to replay() over these lines - the documents, the statuses and the rules alike. Sits at the bottom beside tracker/locking.py and imports only it: the events are plain dicts, so each writer serialises its own rows with the function in tracker/records.py that owns that shape, and no cycle is created. One os.write of the whole line under O_APPEND then fsync, so a kill mid-append leaves at most a torn tail: read_events() ignores it and the next append() truncates it, and nothing else ever rewrites the file. O_APPEND is atomic for concurrent writers on POSIX and is not on Windows, which is why append() refuses unless locking.lock_is_held() says this process holds the engagement lock. Not SQLite: a database file a cloud client syncs is a corrupted database file. migrated is the one event that carries no row - it named the files decision 102's migration moved aside; nothing writes one since 104, and it stays readable. Rows are keyed by the original's PBC location; a row that followed an original the client moved carries the identity it left (was), so the fold drops the vacated one. fold() passes over an event name it does not know and read_events() refuses a bad line anywhere but the tail. The reminder writes files and takes no lock, so drafted is reserved; runner and api reach the writers through the filer, the scanner and the manifest and make no call of their own. The two folds agree by construction and not because no writer here teaches a word twice. The identifier is keyed exactly as each line spells it, because this module sits below records and may not borrow identifier_key (test_layers); the one reader that has to join two spellings of a request, store._check_learned(), folds both sides itself. So the learned table is inside store.check() at last, and the suite's rebuild-and-check fixture proves it after every test. Decision 118 added draft_approved beside drafted: a person read the week's draft in the app and approved it, carrying the stage, the file, that file's header fingerprint and the identifiers asked. Folded by nothing, like drafted - a fact about a week, not a row of the index - and carrying no word of the letter.
