The journal's format is unchanged. Decision 143 added the row event OPENED ('opened'), whose line carries ATTACHMENTS_KEY and SKIPPED_KEY beside the row; the fold keeps the row only. Decision 160 added the row event RENAMED_BY_PERSON ('renamed_by_person'): a person's rename re-wrote the row - its copies renamed in place (moved into the renamed request folder before decision 168), or only its identifier changed; each closes one intent the rename wrote. Decision 157 added two row events: COPY_REMADE ('copy_remade' - a gone working copy made again from its original, by the pass or by a person's Put it back, closing its intent) and ORIGINAL_RETURNED ('original_returned' - a row's own original back from the inbox, moved to its recorded place, no new row); ANSWER_WITHDRAWN_BY_PERSON also records a person marking a both-gone row's own request missing. Both fold like every row event, so the store's version is unchanged. Decision 180: every ValueError a line raises while it is parsed - a number past the interpreter's digit limit included - is the record's LedgerError with its line. Decision 189 (A-9): an OSError from _write_line() or _truncate_torn_tail() leaves as RecordNotWritten(LedgerError) with code = the errno's name and the fixed sentence RECORD_NOT_WRITTEN - the path (a client's folder) stays on __cause__, so the pass catches it as it catches every LedgerError and one full disk costs one household. Decision 187: op_ends(op) says once which end of a step reads and which writes - (from, read) and (to, write) for a copy or a move, (from, write) for a removal - for the filer and the store's gate. STAGE_KEY moved here from reminder (reminder re-exports it) so the gate can bound a draft's stage. Decision 187's review (S1): day_of catches OSError and OverflowError as well as ValueError, so a stamp Windows cannot give a local day reads as long ago. Decision 188: ACCEPTED_KEY ('accepted') with the one value FOLDER_NAME_ACCEPTED ('folder_name') - a person's word that a folder's name is the name, carried only on the household_changed and rules_changed lines the API's accept-folder-name writes; the store admits it there with that value only.

EngagementLock (the open handle and its token), EngagementLockedError; engagement_lock() context manager, taken before the request list, the record or the drop folder is read.

The descriptor stays open while held (Windows then refuses to delete it, so a stale-looking lock its owner still holds is refused) and release_lock() removes the file only if it still carries this run's token. RUN_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS is the one number for how long a scheduled pass may run: tracker.scheduling renders it as the task's ExecutionTimeLimit and STALE_LOCK_SECONDS is derived above it. One machine per clients root: a lock file synced between two machines is not a lock. lock_status()/clear_stale_lock() back the app's lock notice. Decision 54: pid_alive() - a lock whose owner process is gone is stale at any age. Decision 56: the lock line carries host=; another host's pid is unknowable, never dead. Decision 59: a lock that cannot be deleted on release is marked RELEASED_LINE. Decision 102: the lock is not re-entrant - it is an O_EXCL file - so the steps a pass makes take a lock_held flag and skip taking it, and a writer that may be reached with the lock already held (manifest.save_rules(), the journal's append) asks lock_is_held() rather than taking it twice. Decision 115: the machine's name in the lock line comes from platform.node(), not from the socket module - the same name, and the package imports no network module. Decision 137 (L6): the module docstring states that the stale-lock rules rest on the one-machine rule - another host's lock is left to the age rule, whose promise is this machine's schedule's. Decision 171 (the Drive test's F1 and F2): on Google Drive a contended unlink can report success and leave the file, so release_lock() reads the file back - only FileNotFoundError proves it went, a refused read is looked at again - and treats its own token still there like a refused delete (retry, then RELEASED_LINE); the file is read again before every retried delete; a module-level Counter of the exact tokens this process holds (by token, not path: no second spelling hides a held lock, and a release removes only its own), behind a threading.Lock kept as insurance (the app runs one tracker process per command, no threads), makes a lock naming this process whose text is not a held token a leftover to replace - one process takes the same lock twice in ordinary work (an app command then its _rescan; a fed return in two household passes) - while a held token is still refused; and a PermissionError from the O_EXCL create is changing hands only while something is at the name (retried up to _CHANGING_HANDS_ATTEMPTS times, then EngagementLockedError 'is changing hands'): refused with the name free, once more at once, and then the original PermissionError goes to the caller, a run error, never a quiet skip. Decision 189 (SPEC-161 A-F3): acquire_lock() fsyncs the lock line; LockStatus.owner_gone is the one judgement (_owner_gone() reads it too): released; unwritten (empty, no pid=) and older than EMPTY_LOCK_SECONDS (60); or this host's and started more than BOOT_MARGIN_SECONDS (120) before boot_time() (GetTickCount64 on Windows, /proc/uptime elsewhere, None and no boot rule when neither reads; the suite replaces it) or its pid gone. Another host's lock keeps the age rule.

Decision 67: _prior_of() never compares an engagement with itself and matches the engagement sharing the most trailing names only when it is the only one; the walk lists a folder it could not read as a problem row, never a silence (decision 125 turned it into the positional _walk_root()/_walk_private()/_walk_household()/_walk_year(), and a folder it cannot list is the UNLISTED misfit). Decision 68: a Rolled From that matches nothing is a warning the engagement carries (ROLLED_FROM_UNMATCHED); a problem row is never the prior. Decision 104: discovery is by the journal, not by a workbook; engagement_from() reads the details and the rules through the store, catching ManifestError, LedgerError and StoreError - and, named by type, any other exception one synced record raises - into the problem, so one folder cannot end the pass inside discovery; a folder whose record carries no rules beside the legacy workbook is listed the same way as one with no record (an engagement created before decision 103 whose rules never reached the journal). Nothing imports such a folder, by the owner's word: it is set up again in the app. This is the one reader of LEGACY_MANIFEST_FILENAME in the package. It imports store and ledger (L1) from L3, which the layers allow. Decision 131: _prior_of() reads layout.shared_tail and layout.ROLLED_FROM_TAIL (moved there from _shared_tail/_TAIL_NAMES so the scaffold reads the same rule); _same_folder stays here because it resolves, which layer 0 must not. Decision 177: the record wins for what a return is (its label, its year, its prior); where anything is written is positional, and a return rolls forward where it sits. Decision 188: _skip reads layout.MACHINE_PREFIXES (the one list; the name rule refuses every such name), and a household or return folder whose name the layout's rule refuses is MISFIT_BAD_NAME with the rule's reason - the constructors would refuse a path through it, so the pass never reaches it. Decision 188: _walk_root tells the two trees apart by layout.place_of (CLIENTS / PRIVATE), never by comparing a tree word; the CLI's root is door.checked_root. Decision 188 (part 3): the folder is the identity and the record's labels are a claim. NAME_DISAGREES and _disagreement are gone (overruled with decision 177's warning and 125's 'the record wins'): discover_engagements fills Registry.paused (household -> households.HOUSEHOLD_PAUSED or HOUSEHOLD_PAUSED_YEAR, from households.pause_of over the household's record and its readable returns) and Registry.stopped (TWO_CLAIM for every household whose folder or claimed name is another's by layout.name_key - a copy of a household folder - and HOUSEHOLD_RECORD_MISSING for a household position whose record is gone while its returns hold theirs; those returns are listed as engagements carrying the sentence, so the pass counts them as failed). _walk_root lists the client tree's first level by name with os.scandir (never deeper, never a stat of what is inside) and every Clients folder that is no discovered household's is MISFIT_CLIENT_NO_RECORD; MISFIT_NO_HOUSEHOLD_RECORD is corrected (the app will not set a household up over it). Review of 188: held_back(household_dir) is the one question a new return and every Roll Forward ask - stopped (record gone, TWO_CLAIM), paused, or its client folder gone - with the pass's own sentence (M3, S4); client folders are matched to households by layout.name_key (S5). Re-check of 188 (R1, correcting S5): a client folder is a household's when its name matches under os.path.normcase, as the file system compares; one that matches only by layout.name_key is MISFIT_CLIENT_LOOK_ALIKE - listed, never adopted or read. The key refuses; it never identifies.

Decision 108: the command line takes page.tolerant_console() first (its report carries an arrow a cp1252 console cannot encode, and it used to die after the record was written and before the folders were made, with a second run refused), and does all of its work - create_engagement(), then scaffold_engagement() when asked - before it prints a line, so nothing about the report can leave a folder with a record and no scaffold. Decision 123: with_default_dates() lives here, beside the carry rule that clears the two dates, so both ways of building next year's engagement fill them - the command line wraps carry_engagement_info() in it (the form the prior recorded, else the one asked for, and the target year) and tracker.api imports it for create and rollover; the defaulting used to live in the API alone, and the command line's engagements came out with no Due Date at all. Decision 126: roll_household() is the household's loop and roll_forward() stays the primitive it calls, so one return still rolls on its own; each rolled return is created under its own lock by create_engagement() and a refusal on one (an existing target, the path limit through filer.refuse_a_path_past_the_limit(), a year not after the prior's) lands in HouseholdRollover.skipped with its sentence and undoes none of the others. A return that was ticked is never retired by the loop - rolled, its successor's Rolled From retires it; refused, it is still this year's work. The client's side is laid out once at the end (scaffold_household()), so the inbox README lists the new year's lists the day the firm rolls. The CLI carries both forms in one __main__, told apart by store.kind() - a household folder takes --year with --all or --only and prints ROLLED / NOT ROLLED / RETIRED, a return folder is the per-return form unchanged. Decision 137 (L5): carried_link() drops a household link that is not a web address with LINK_NOT_CARRIED (RolloverReport.link_dropped), rather than refusing the roll; the API carries it to the app. Decision 144: _carry() carries short_title (years shifted); a blank one takes the template row's only while the document is still the template's. Decision 177: a return rolls forward where it sits - _roll_one and the command line compute the target from the household being rolled and the prior's folder name, never from the names its record carries, and write those names into next year's record; the command line prints the prior's NAME_DISAGREES as a WARNING line. Decision 188: a rolled return is unique by the layout's key in the target household-year (households.return_name_taken), and the command line's --only reads a return by name_key. Decision 188: the CLI reads its folder through door.household_dir, else door.return_dir, so a folder in the client tree is neither whatever journal is in it. Decision 188 (part 3): roll_household and both forms of the command line refuse a paused household (households.household_pause) before anything is written.
- **`tracker/router.py`** — Decides which single manifest row a dropped file belongs to. Evidence order: required keywords, then any-keywords/period, read off a text layer or off OCR (OCR routes on required keywords only). There is no third tier: a file name is never evidence for a filing (decision 92), and a document nothing could be read out of parks. The router knows no person (decision 128): whose document this is is asked by the household pass against the return's own people list, not here.
  - CLI: `python -m tracker.router`
  - constants: `UNMATCHED` = 'matched no request', `AMBIGUOUS` = 'matched more than one request', `OCR_ONLY` = 'matched only by OCR text', `NO_REQUEST_ACCEPTS` = 'no request accepts .{extension} files', `CONTESTED_PREFIX` = 'looks like'
  - imports: `tracker/__init__.py`, `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/reasons.py`, `tracker/records.py`, `tracker/validators.py`
  - used by: `tools/backtest.py`, `tracker/filer.py`
  - imports at call time: `tracker/door.py`, `tracker/page.py`
  - enforces: `rule:nothing-is-guessed`
  - tested by: `tests/test_router.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/test_build.py`, `tests/test_catalog.py`, `tests/test_content_check.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_irs_forms.py`, `tests/test_real_corpus.py`, `tests/test_records.py`, `tests/test_review.py`, `tests/test_rollover.py`
  - note: Reads the document through content_check.extract() - the scanner's reading - and leaves its per-row verdicts among the engagement's verdicts in the store (content_check.ContentCache) keyed by content, so the scan finds them under the working copy's name. Every scan with no text layer is OCR'd, whatever its name says, and OCR text routes only on required keywords - an any-keyword match on OCR text is OCR_ONLY, a lead for a person, because a misread word is how a document lands under the wrong request. One PdfVerdictCache per file (or the caller's) so a PDF is parsed once, not once per row. The CLI (python -m tracker.router <engagement> <files>) says where each file would go and why, moving nothing. Extension alone never routes. A document matching one row's required keywords but failing its other rules is contested and blocks its own filing — misfiling a tax document is worse than not filing it. When nothing routes, the reason is the most useful one available: a document whose content fits a row that refused the file (size floor, type, unreadable PDF) is reported as CONTESTED_PREFIX, and a file every row refused for the same reason carries that reason. A file name is read the same whole-token way a keyword is, run-together spelling and all (W2 for W-2), but only ever as evidence for a person. Eligibility is has_routing_rules(): keywords or a typed year; a year derived from Period only checks a document a keyword already matched. Decision 55, as decision 92 left it: a text layer extract() marked needs_ocr is no text at all, so a multi-page scan is read no further than a one-page one - and where 55 then filed it on its name, it now parks. Decision 58: no run-together fallback; the keyword pattern already reads a dash or space as optional. Decision 73: a row whose any-keywords all matched and whose year alone failed is remembered as a lead, and a file that would otherwise be parked with 'matched no request' is parked as 'looks like J01 (expected period not found ...)' with J01 as its candidate - the sentence a contested file gets, so the reminder asks the client about the period. A lead pre-empts no filing, unlike a required-keyword match, so the decision is exactly as it was; only the reason and the candidates improve. The Routing record and EVIDENCE_CONTENT live in tracker/records.py (decision 100) and are re-exported here for one release: the decision is a record, this module is the deciding. Decision 82: Routing.evidence_record is why, beside Routing.evidence, the tier the decision rested on - EVIDENCE_CONTENT or nothing, since decision 92 removed EVIDENCE_FILENAME (nothing rests on a name; content_check.RULE_FILENAME, the word an index row actually carries, is untouched and still produced). Keyed by candidate identifier: the content check's own Evidence tuple for a row that was read, _filename_evidence() for what the name said (a name is all title and has no page), and _refusal_evidence() for a tier-2 refusal, which travels as reasons.Reason.code rather than the sentence a person reads. _recorded_for() cuts it down to the identifiers the decision names, because every row considered leaves something behind and one index cell must not carry the whole manifest's workings. It decides nothing: every verdict is reached exactly as it was before there was a record. Decision 84: a blocked file - content fits a row, the same row's tier-2 rules refused the file - keeps the verdict's evidence beside the refusal in record, because the refusal alone says which rule said no and never which request the document looked like. The verdict was already read there to decide the file was blocked, so nothing is computed twice and no placement moves. Decision 117: a tier-2 refusal on a file nothing could be read out of - a locked PDF, an empty upload - is asked what its NAME says, exactly as an unreadable scan is, and the name's evidence is recorded beside the refusal for the person who has to open it (and for the reminder's hold, which reads the review shortlist). The decision does not move an inch: no candidate, the same reason, nothing filed on a name. Decision 92, the owner's (2026-09-18): A DOCUMENT NOBODY CAN READ IS FILED BY NOBODY. The by-name tier is gone - when no word of the file could be read (a scan with no text layer OCR could not rescue, an image-only PDF, an empty sheet) no row is a candidate, and the file parks with reasons.NO_READABLE_TEXT (router.UNREADABLE), which is deliberately not UNMATCHED: nothing was matched against anything, and the fix is OCR or a person, never another keyword. _filename_evidence() stays and is recorded on the parked row, so review.triage() offers the request the name points at at RULE_STRENGTH's weakest tier and the app's card and the Status Report show it - a place for a person to start reading, never a filing. _read() no longer skips OCR for a sensibly named scan: nothing is filed on a name, so OCR is the only thing that can still file one, and the scan whose name says W-2 is exactly the one whose content must be read (the _filename_hit shortcut went with the skip). The cost was stated and accepted: until OCR was installed every scanned PDF parked (since decision 169 the reader ships in the app) - twelve rows of the firm's own corpus moved from filing to parking, and two the name had been misfiling now park instead. Decision 93 (a row per issuer): an issuer row is an ordinary row carrying the entity's name in Required Keywords, and which row wins needed no new rule - a required keyword is the strongest tier and the generic K-1 row has none, so the issuer row takes the K-1 that names it. The one rule added is the park: when any row narrows the row that accepted a document (manifest.narrowing_rows over the rows this pass considers, so an issuer row set aside as Override.NOT_APPLICABLE is nobody's issuer) and none of the narrowing rows matched, nothing is filed - reasons.ISSUER_NOT_NAMED, the narrowing rows named, shortlist led by the row that did accept it. Filing on the generic row would put two entities' K-1s in one folder; taking the row left over would be guessing by elimination. Decision 107: whether a page counts two forms as its own is content_check.own_forms(), the same reading the scanner's miss path makes; computed once in route_file() and handed to evaluate_rules() for the ordinary reading and to the split alike, so a page that prints two forms' own names never files on a third form it merely mentions (decision 94's rule, by construction); the forms are then taken in first-mention order (self_named_forms) for the filing order, and _multi_form() decides exactly as before. Decision 105: the split's verdicts are remembered too. _multi_form() takes route_file()'s keep closure and calls it for every row it files a copy under, with the second reading's verdict, after the ordinary reading has left its own refusal - the verdict the router files on is the one the scan must find, or the second copy fails validation on the next pass and the client is asked for a form they already sent. A page that parks keeps nothing new. Decision 128 gave route_file() a `reading` argument in place of `text`: the household pass reads each drop once (read_once()) and routes that one Extraction against every return it feeds, so a two-return household costs one reading rather than two, and from_ocr travels with it so decision 50's stricter rule still applies. Decision 127 changed no rule here: a photo arrives with from_ocr set, so decision 50's stricter reading applies to it unchanged, and route_file() only became two functions - itself, which makes the two refusals that must come before any reading (a cloud placeholder is never read, a Google stub is never a document) and then stamps Routing.seconds on whatever _decide() returns, and _decide(), which is the whole decision as it was. The seconds decide nothing; they let the pass name its slowest documents. Decision 137: route_file() parks a file past validators.MAX_READ_MB before any reading, with reasons.TOO_LARGE as its whole reason, and a parked file read from a cut text says so (reasons.TEXT_CUT). Decision 141: a signed return of the wrong year - a row asks_for_a_return() whose required keywords matched and whose only failure is its period - contests and parks even when another row matched strongly (this year's 1065 with its K-1s, a 1040 with a W-2G stapled behind it); return rows only, checked before the ordinary contested rule. DECISION 140: a read document that reaches the last exit (UNMATCHED) still points somewhere when a row's own form number is shown on the page - a RULE_REQUIRED/RULE_ANY evidence whose term content_check.form_key() reads as a form, said in the title, or on the first page (dominant) AND beside at least one more of the row's own keywords - dominance alone is not enough, a misread K-1's two 'W-2 wages' lines make W-2 dominant (_shows_its_form_number) - or, where no row's is, when the file's name says a row's keyword (_filename_evidence, the unreadable scan's hint): _near_miss() parks it with reasons.SHOWS_ITS_FORM_NUMBER (or, on the name's path, reasons.NAME_POINTS_AT - its own sentence, 'file name', because the page showed nothing) and those rows as the evidence record, NEVER as candidates, so a list where that row is the only one still parks. Only rows whose tier-2 rules let the file through are asked. A01's three required phrases were deliberately not loosened: every looser rule filed the W-3 family and the W-2c as W-2s. The split's self-named forms are self_named, no longer a reuse of the file-name list named. Decision 146: a broker's consolidated 1099 that several rows accept on their any-keywords files whole under the one row accepted BECAUSE OF its 1099-B section (_explained_by over the evidence, never an identifier; content_check.carries_a_1099b_section says the page carries one), after the issuer rule and never on OCR's word; two such rows or none and it parks. The other asked rows that accepted it ride on Routing.answers - no copy - and become the filed row's Also Answers cell. Reads no word of a document since decision 189. read_once(path, questions) is the router's one judge_bounded call per drop, asked about every considered row (questions_for) plus the filer's name questions. _decide and _multi_form read the Judgment (row verdicts, required_matched, any_matched, own, self_named, carries_1099b, has_words) where they read words; _required_matched moved to content_check as required_matched. route_file takes judgment= from the pass or reading= from a tool, which it judges in-process with judgment_of. A stopped or crashed judgment is kept under every considered row's fingerprint and the open-test fingerprint (_keep_the_stop, ruling 3.4), as the scanner already kept it; a transient one never is. _filename_evidence still reads only the file's name.

Decision 102: run_engagement() holds ONE engagement lock across scaffold, file, scan and view, and tells each step the lock is held; a dry run takes none; a lock it cannot get is a skip. Decision 115: _draft_step() runs the gate - a held draft writes nothing, _retire_unedited_drafts() removes the run's own unedited drafts and leaves an edited one, run.held counts the rows and run.draft_note is the refusal (in the console, the log and the practice page's Drafted cell as STATUS_HELD); --reminders always is held too (decision 13 amended). Every draft step ends in _record(): one DRAFTED event through the reminder's record_draft() under the pass's lock, only when something changed or the week's draft is a new week's. last_drafted() answers from the last DRAFTED that wrote a file, and falls back to the files' times for a journal from before 115; draft_is_held() says whether the record's last word is a hold, and should_draft(held=True) drafts on the first pass after the hold clears, first draft or not. Decision 118: a draft a person approved in the app is protected for the rest of that draft week exactly as an edited one is - _draft_step() hands last_draft_day() to write_draft(), _retire_unedited_drafts() and _refresh_stale_draft() as approved_since, EngagementRun carries approved, and _drafted_cell() says APPROVED_NOTE where it would say the stage. The draft day stays the runner's (decision 12): the reminder module is below this one and is handed the week rather than working it out. Decision 129 gave run_household() the registry, so the feed list resolves to this year's returns and the pass takes every lock it needs - its own and the fed ones - in layout.lock_order_key order. A feed that resolves to nothing rides every own return's warnings; a fed return is judged and filed into but never scanned, drafted or drawn here, because that is its own household's pass to make. Since decision 204 the pass files nothing into a fed return (a document only a fed return wants parks in this household's queue, counted as under review until a person hands it over), so FILED_INTO_FED and its emission in _sort_step are gone. Decision 127: EngagementRun.slowest is the filing report's list of slow readings, and summary() adds SLOW_READING_NOTE for the slowest when it passed SLOW_READING_SECONDS (20.0) - a line the run says, not a limit it enforces; nothing anywhere cuts a reading short, because the benchmark and the owner's speed ceiling are measured in exactly these seconds. In a household the reading is said once, on the first own return's line. Decision 132: A PASS NEEDS THE PRACTICE - run_household()'s registry is required, so Run now and the schedule cannot differ by construction, and a None registry (a root that could not be walked) is refused on every run with NO_PRACTICE and nothing is touched; _feeds_of() says FEEDS_UNREAD on every own return when the household's own record will not read, rather than feeding nothing in silence; _sort_step() hands the sort own= and fed= by name. Decision 131: THE PASS MEASURES BEFORE IT READS - _no_room() runs after _worth_a_pass (which now keeps the loaded list on EngagementRun.items, so the room is measured without a second read) and before the locks: ROOM_PARKS rides the warnings (and the page's Warnings column and the run's lines); a return merely short of room (ROOM_SHORT) is NOT warned (the lead's L-1: names are cut, everything files, and a warning always on is read by nobody) and is still sorted, its names cut to fit; a return whose floor passes the limit skips the WHOLE household with HOUSEHOLD_NO_ROOM, the held-lock shape - nothing read, locked, scaffolded, scanned, drafted or drawn. Decision 137 Part B: READING_STOP_PAGE_SECONDS and READING_STOP_DOCUMENT_SECONDS are named beside SLOW_READING_SECONDS (the reader, content_check, owns them): a slow reading is named, one past the stop is abandoned. Decision 176: a root typed on the command line is held to settings.clients_root_refusal() exactly as the saved one is, so no caller - a person's or another program's - can hand a pass the system drive or the folder holding the settings. Decision 189 (the cheap core): main() makes the RunReport and run_registry(report=) fills it as each household finishes, so a pass stopped by the runner's own code (PASS_STOPPED, by class) still hands the log and the page what finished; the console, append_log (LOG_NOT_WRITTEN onto the page), the page and store.close() each run in a guard of their own, and a stopped pass or an unwritten log exits 1. The page's problems list leads with the pass's own sentences (status_report(warnings=)); the run log carries each return's warnings as a count, never their words; _engagement_status() catches ManifestError, LedgerError, StoreError and OSError per row, so one bad record costs one row. should_draft(created=) owes a never-drafted return its first draft once a draft day has come since created_on() - the day of its first rules event (SPEC-161 A-F8). PAGE_NOT_WRITTEN is the page's failure sentence for the app's reply. Decision 189 (the bounded household): run_household() never raises - its pre-checks are inside the guard - and has budget seconds (HOUSEHOLD_BUDGET_SECONDS, 15 min, on ocr.awake_clock) handed to the sort and the scan as a deadline; a household out of time says OUT_OF_TIME on every working return, drafts nothing (OUT_OF_TIME_NO_DRAFT) and still refreshes its README; Run now gets the same budget. run_registry() takes households least recently completed first from PASS_ORDER_FILENAME beside the store (a hint: missing is the walk's order, unreadable adds ORDER_HINT_UNREADABLE; started/ended marks put a household a pass was killed in last), retries once at the end a household whose every working return was locked_out, and names a household not served two passes running (NOT_SERVED_TWICE), which main() exits as NOT_SERVED_TWICE_EXIT_CODE (3). A logged pass appends PASS_STARTED_LINE first, after saying PASS_DID_NOT_FINISH when the log's last start has no summary after it. Decision 188: the CLI's root, typed or saved, is door.checked_root (one level too deep refused too); _under uses layout.parts_below. Decision 188 (part 3): run_household touches nothing of a household in registry.stopped or registry.paused - no sweep, layout, sort, scan, draft or README - and every run of it carries the sentence as its error (red, exit 1, every pass until a person acts: D-9's part); a household whose client folder is gone when households.client_side_expected says it had one fails with CLIENT_FOLDER_MISSING and nothing is made. format_report ends every pass with the misfits under 'Folders the tracker leaves alone'.

The scan calls filer.ensure() first, inside its own lock, so the store holds the engagement it is about to record to and the rules it works from are the ones the record holds (decision 104: the ones the app's editor last saved). Decision 60: a person's acceptance is the newest row for the location and its recorded bytes. Decision 62: a person's filing waives tier 2 too. Imports the filer's index reader at call time; the filer imports this module at call time inside _rescan() - the deliberate cycle, stated on the filer's node. Decision 109: the scan reads the index once (_the_index()) and acts on what the filer's sweep decided under the same lock - it writes no row of its own. _wandered() is the paths FILE_MOVED rows name as their copies' whereabouts, and _scan_item() drops those from a request's files before the tiers, because a mislaid copy is not the request's whatever its bytes say; _claimed_paths() is every working copy the record names, newest row per location, and a claimed path holding other bytes is _a_stranger_at(), written as reasons.COPY_CHANGED on the row and by _changed_copy_warnings() on ScanReport.warnings (decision 3 extended; since decision 155 such a copy is NOT counted - a working copy whose bytes disagree with its original is treated as not there, so a torn copy never makes a request Received and the firm-side note keeps the letter from asking the client). A FILE_MOVED row whose home is a place this request's copies sit (directly in Prepared, named for it) writes reasons.FILE_MOVED. Both facts go in before the failures, so the note's cut can never take a firm-side marker off the end, and neither is a failure - a moved copy leaves the request Missing, not Failed Validation. _filed_by_a_person() and the de-duplication hash through ContentCache.digest_of() now, so this module holds no sha256_of at all, and prune() keeps every file under Prepared/ rather than only what a request claims - a memo dropped for a parked copy or a stray was a file read again every pass. the pattern helper moved down to tracker/records.py as as_pattern(), where both readers of a written sentence share it; the regression read-back of decision 108 is unchanged. Decision 119: _interrupted() is the second thing the scan keeps out of a request's count - where a step that died half way was putting a working copy, and the sentence the row it parked carries. The wreck of a copy the power cut in half is nobody's document, so it is not counted and the row's own firm-side sentence goes on the request instead, which is what makes the request read Missing rather than Failed Validation for a document the client sent perfectly well. Decision 146: _answered() reads each Filed / File Moved row's Also Answers cell, and a request a consolidated statement answers counts it as one document per section that answered it (records.answer_count), with reasons.IN_CONSOLIDATED on its notes and no file of its own read; a person takes one back with filer.mark_missing_again (one answer_withdrawn_by_person row event). Decision 168: a request's files are assign_files()'s - the files directly in Prepared whose names belong to it - checked by validators.check_files(); NO_REQUEST_FOLDER and FOLDERS_NOTE are gone and a request with nothing is simply Missing; the warnings are UNCLAIMED_FILE (a file whose name begins with no identifier) and reasons.PERSONS_FOLDER (each folder other than the review folder, once per pass). Decision 157: _scan_item says reasons.COPY_MISSING of a claimed copy under the request's name that is absent on a row that is not File Moved (the sweep could not make it again this pass), and reasons.COPY_AND_ORIGINAL_GONE instead of reasons.FILE_MOVED for a filer.both_gone() row - both firm-side, so a missing copy is never a client ask by itself. _answered(engagement_dir, rows, cache) carries why a consolidated host is not counted (_host_not_counted: its copy missing, not the one filed, nowhere, or gone with its original; a wanderer or a placeholder still counts), and an answer from such a host counts nothing and says reasons.ANSWER_NOT_COUNTED (ANSWERED_BY, the ANSWER_WHY_* words) in place of IN_CONSOLIDATED. Decision 189: scan_engagement() saves the verdict cache after each request (a no-op when nothing changed), so a pass killed mid-scan reads again only what it was killed on. Decision 189 (the bounded household, ruling 2.2): scan_engagement(deadline=) sets it on the scan's ContentCache for the loop, and only a cache miss past it stops the scan (content_check.OutOfTime, raised before a judgment starts): a request whose verdicts are all kept is scanned whatever the time; from the first request that would read, no further request is scanned or recorded - each keeps the status the record holds - and ScanReport.unreached counts them. Decision 189 (the judgment worker): the open test on a cache miss (content_check.open_verdict(path, cache, item)) judges the working copy's own row in the same child job; the content check that follows takes the held Judgment, so a working copy costs one trip to the child, and the scanner holds no document text (it held up to 8 whole texts before).

- **`tracker/store.py`** — The store: one SQLite file per clients root (STORE_FILENAME) on the designated machine's local disk, beside the settings file, holding engagements, requests, statuses, learned_keywords, documents and events for every engagement under that root, all folded from the journal and from nothing else - and, since decision 107, the two tables of the tier-3 verdict cache, VERDICTS_TABLE and FILE_MEMOS_TABLE, which are NOT the record's: derived from the bytes and the rules, never journalled, left empty by a rebuild and never compared by check(). Owns the file name, the schema and its user_version (bumped by decision 104 when the workbook digest column left, by 107 when the cache's two tables arrived, by 116 for override_reason, by 117 for the Filing Deadline column and by 119 for the intents table), path_for(), open(), connect() / close() (one connection per process, to the file TRACKER_STORE names or the one beside the settings file), documents(), rules(), statuses(), learned_keywords() and engagement_info() (what the readers answer from), record() (the journal first, then one immediate transaction), sync(), catch_up() and follow_the_journal() (replay the lines the store has not applied, building the engagement from the journal alone where it has none; catch_up() is filer.ensure()'s, by count, and a look that finds nothing to apply takes no lock), rebuild_engagement() (delete and build again from the journal), cached_verdicts() and remember_verdicts() (the verdict cache's one read and one write - the write is its own immediate transaction under the engagement lock, never record()), forget() (drop a failed create's row), check() (every disagreement with the journal, as sentences), state() (current / behind / unknown, from the journal's head alone), export() (three CSVs on demand, every cell text, a cell that begins like a formula behind an apostrophe) and the CLI that rebuilds, checks, exports or states a whole clients root - its first argument read by store_named(): the app folder, the settings file in it, or the store file itself, and anything else refused so a typo never creates a store; a store open() refuses is said in its one sentence with exit 1, never a traceback (decision 107).

  - note: Decision 101 built it and had nothing read it; 102 moved the index into it; 103 the statuses and the person's rules; 104 took away the last thing that was passed in from anywhere else. WHERE IT LIVES IS THE POINT: never under the clients root and never in an engagement folder, because those sync and a synced database file is a corrupted one - decision 87's finding, kept, with the owner's 2026-09-19 decision adding the local database the other side of that line. The journal stays in the folder and travels with the engagement; the store is local and disposable, and the arrow only points one way - the store is rebuilt from the journal, never the reverse. THE GUARANTEE is journal-then-apply: record() refuses outside the engagement lock and refuses a retired event name by sentence, appends each event through append() and only then folds them in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so a machine that dies between the two leaves the journal ahead and sync() replays the difference. The fold has one owner, apply() in tracker/ledger.py, so a line-at-a-time replay and a whole-file fold cannot differ. ONE CONNECTION PER PROCESS: connect() opens it on first use and every writer deep in the package asks for it by name; close() lets it go, which Windows needs before a database file can be deleted. TRACKER_STORE overrides where it is - the suite points every test at its own file. It imports records, ledger and locking and nothing else of the package at load time - narrower than its layer allows, so the database the readers answer from never depends on the modules that walk folders and move files; connect() reads tracker/settings.py at call time and the CLI imports the registry at call time to find the folders. The gate is check(), run by the autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py over every engagement the suite leaves behind: the documents and the rules are compared with ledger.replay() over the journal, always - an engagement with no rules event has none on either side - and the statuses and taught keywords with the same lines folded by the store's case rule (decision 136). Decision 104: the requests table is the fold of rules_changed (and of the rules_imported lines older journals carry, which _apply_rules_event folds the same way); rules() returns [] for an engagement the store holds and None only for one it does not; has_rules_event() is what a save is a difference from; rebuild_engagement() takes nothing but the journal (the workbook-fed fallback, the sequence number workbook rows were marked with, the digest column and its bookkeeping all went, and the schema guard that refused a request row whose fields had moved is a test in tests/test_store.py now); state() has one stamp, the journal's head, because a rules edit is an event; forget() is what a failed create leaves behind - nothing - and writes nothing to any journal. A version-1 file is refused by the sentence open() has always had, and is deleted and rebuilt: the store is disposable and no store at the office predates this chain. key_root() is the one rule for the key an engagement is stored under (root_for() is its name for a caller with no root in hand): the root the settings file names whenever the folder is under it - the record's own root, which wins over the root a caller typed, so a pass run on one client's folder and a check given the drive key the engagement as the app does - else the caller's root, else the root a return's position names (decision 134: four levels up, when its parent is a year folder and its household sits in the private tree, asked of layout at call time - so two years of one return are two rows on a machine or in a reader with no root in hand), else, only for a folder outside that layout, the folder's parent. _engagement_row() answers by that exact key, and under the recorded root by nothing else: a folder there with no row is one the store has not met, never another engagement whose key its path ends with (decision 106; the pre-integration audit found Clients/Archive/Smith 2025 answered as Clients/Smith 2025's row). The tail - the one stored path the folder ends with, longest wins - answers only where no recorded root covers the folder, which is decision 103's end-to-end finding on a machine with no settings file. Decision 107: the verdict cache's two tables are per engagement and cascade with it; cached_verdicts() returns the memos and the verdicts at the CACHE_VERSION the caller names as plain dicts and JSON text (this module never learns the verdict's record - test_layers pins that it imports nothing above it); remember_verdicts() deletes the rows at other versions, the paths and digests pruned, and upserts what was learned, refusing outside the lock and for an unknown engagement by the two sentences record() uses (_held_under_the_lock()). A version-2 file is refused by the same sentence a version-1 file was. RULE_COLUMNS is built from records.RULE_FIELDS; _rule_from_sql() hands the list fields back as lists and the flag as a boolean, the shape the API hands the editor. Decision 115: last_event() answers the newest event of a name for an engagement (or the newest carrying a key) from the events table - what the reminder compares this week's draft with, and what the runner reads the last draft day from. Decision 112: document_seqs() reads back what _apply() has always written - which journal line last wrote each index row - keyed through the recorded root as documents() is, {} for an engagement the store does not hold, no lock (a read). It is the freshness handle the app carries out with the row and a person's action carries back; per row rather than the engagement's head, so a scan between the card and the click refuses nothing. A rebuild numbers the same lines the same way, so the mapping survives it. Decision 113: _apply() deletes a learned_keywords row on a keyword_unlearned event, keyed by identifier_key and the keyword exactly, as the insert keys it; _check_learned() holds the table to ledger.Folded.learned - the table's words in seq order against the journal's fold, both sides folded through identifier_key first, one sentence per request that differs - and check() appends it, so the one part of this database the record could not vouch for is in the gate. _refuse_a_malformed_line() checks a keyword event for the first time: both events must name a request and a word, both text and neither blank, because a keyword that is not text was written into the table as the text of whatever it carried while the journal's fold kept the value itself, which is a disagreement the check would now report and nobody could act on. Decision 119: SCHEMA_VERSION 6 and the intents table - the fold of the moving lines, one row per key, holding the whole line - written by _apply() as each line is met and deleted by any row event naming the key (or by move_abandoned); open_intents() reads them back oldest first for the filer's recovery and for the refusal a person's action makes while one is open; _check_intents() holds the table to ledger.replay()'s own fold, so a rebuild gives the same open set and the gate would say which key they disagreed about; _refuse_a_malformed_line() learns the moving shape, because a recovery acts on it with a file already half moved, and (decision 126) the sharing_confirmed shape, which is no shape at all: that event carries nothing but its stamp, so a line of it carrying anything is another version's or a hand-written one and is refused by name rather than kept where a reader would trust it. The store's version did not move for it - it is folded by nothing and read back out of the events by last_event(). Version 8 (decision 128) added the return's people to engagements as JSON text and the named mark to requests; _to_sql writes a list with sorted keys, as the journal writes a line, so the column and the fold of the same people are one text and check() compares like with like. A rules_changed line whose people this version cannot read - an unknown kind, a one-word spelling - is refused by name before a value of it reaches a table. Decision 129 put the household's feed list into the household columns as JSON text and moved the schema to version 9; the malformed-line guard learned the feeds' shape. Decision 132 moved the schema to version 10 with no column change, because the fold changed: a released line (ledger.RELEASE_EVENTS) deletes the row under its key and closes its intent in _apply(), exactly as ledger.apply() does, and a version-9 file may hold Handed Over rows this version never produces. The guard requires a released line's key and refuses a row on it, and refuses a moving line carrying decision 129's also_in by name (ALSO_IN) - an intent whose second half this version cannot write must not be recovered as if it had none. Decision 134 moved the schema to version 11 with no column change, because the key changed: a version-10 file may hold two years of one return as one row, keyed by the return's name alone. DECISION 135, A READ NEVER OUTRUNS A WRITE: readers take no lock and the app's process and the pass's share the store, so every function that applies journal lines reads the row, the lines and the head inside its own BEGIN IMMEDIATE and takes the lines and the head from ONE read (ledger.read_with_head()): sync(), catch_up() (follow_the_journal()'s slow path and filer.ensure()'s) and record()'s apply through one helper, _catch_up(), and rebuild_engagement() through the same one read. A look that finds nothing to apply takes no lock: sync() and catch_up() first read the row and the journal outside any transaction and return when the applied seq already equals the journal's lines, and only a decision to write takes BEGIN IMMEDIATE and reads both again inside (_look_then_catch_up(); the look's parsed lines are reused there only when the file still digests to the look's head) - so the app's views, the Status Report and dry runs never queue a pass's record() behind the lock. A stored head therefore always names exactly the lines applied. record() applies what the journal holds past the store's applied_seq as it is inside the transaction, not the batch it was handed. follow_the_journal()'s head fast path stays outside any transaction and parses nothing; filer.ensure() calls catch_up(), which compares by count, so a store an earlier build left with a matching head and a short applied_seq (the stuck return: current by its head, every writer refused) is repaired by the next pass with no rebuild and no version change. Decision 136: check() folds the record's statuses and learned keywords from the journal's lines itself, keyed by identifier_key in journal order (_recorded_statuses, _recorded_learned), rather than taking ledger.replay()'s, which keys them by each line's spelling - so a request respelled by case is one request to the gate, as it is to the store. Decision 137 (L4): MALFORMED_LINE says "line N of the record is malformed"; _refuse_a_malformed_line() gained the ROW_EVENTS branch (a key that is text, a row that is a mapping, a was that is a location) and holds every rule's list fields to lists of words; _write_rule() and _rule_from_sql() hold them to the same shape where a row is written and read. Decision 137 (A3, store version 12): engagements.applied_digest holds the running chain over exactly the lines applied (ledger.read_with_chain / chain_at); _refuse_a_rewrite() proves that prefix in _look_then_catch_up's no-lock look (equal counts with a different chain refuses, never 'nothing to do'), in _catch_up, and in record() before it appends, with REWRITTEN; check() names it; the rebuild computes it. It never repairs itself: the check, then a rebuild. Decision 138: _apply() writes a batch's statuses from _recorded_statuses(events) - one row per identifier_key, the last scan's status, the seq from status_seqs - not from ledger.Folded.statuses, which is keyed by the exact spelling and, written in insertion order, left the second of A01, a01, A01 standing on a rebuild, a sync()/catch_up() top-up or one record() of several scans. The writer and check() now read the one rule; Folded.statuses is unchanged (ledger cannot fold case) and nothing written or shown reads it. SCHEMA_VERSION 14 (decision 143): the documents table gained container. Decision 189 (A-9): open() hands SQLite a connection factory, _Connection (with _Cursor), the one choke point every statement goes through, so every sqlite3.Error leaves the module as StoreUnavailable(StoreError) with code = the SQLite error's name (SQLITE_ERROR when it has none) and the fixed sentence STORE_UNAVAILABLE; the engine's text stays on __cause__ and is never quoted. Decision 187: _refuse_a_malformed_line(event, seq, where, *, kind) is the one admission - every value by the records value rule (stamp_problem on 'at', rule_row_problem, info_problem, entry_problem, status_problem, household_problem, digests, the drafted stage) and every location by layout.place_problem (asked at call time), labels by layout.segment_problem, a moving line refused in a household's record (kind), and each 'also' event admitted by the same rule. Its phrases name the field and the class, never the value. record() runs it on every event before the first ledger.append ('; nothing was written'), _apply() on every line read in (kind from the engagements row) and check() over every line of every journal, so a line applied under the old gate is named without a rebuild. SCHEMA_VERSION is not bumped: a bump would discard the verdict cache for what check() gives. Decision 187's review: a removal is placed with removes=True (M4); keys, 'was' and locations use records.name_problem (M5); an event name this version does not know is said as UNKNOWN_EVENT and a sharing_confirmed line's extra fields are not named (S2). Decision 188: engagement_path and _recorded_root_over use layout.parts_below and _positional_root asks layout.place_of (all at call time, so store still imports only records, ledger and locking at load); the CLI reads its root through door.checked_root and --engagement through door.return_dir or household_dir. Decision 188 (part 3): the admission gate admits ledger.ACCEPTED_KEY only on RULES_CHANGED and HOUSEHOLD_CHANGED and only with FOLDER_NAME_ACCEPTED, refusing any other use without quoting the value. Decision 188 (part 4, SPEC-162 rulings 5 and 6): a truncated journal is refused with TRUNCATED (restore from Drive's trash or version history first; what a rebuild would discard); check() of an engagement whose journal is gone is one JOURNAL_GONE sentence and gone_journals(conn, root) names every stored engagement under the root whose journal is absent - the CLI's check adds them to the one report beside decision 187's re-judging; only_in_the_store lists the applied lines the journal no longer holds, from the events table, and rebuild_engagement(..., discard=False) raises WouldDiscard (WOULD_DISCARD, with the lines) unless discard, returning what it discarded; the CLI's rebuild lists them and exits 1 until --discard. SCHEMA_VERSION 17 (decision 204): the documents table gained waits_for; a version-16 file is refused, deleted and rebuilt from the journals.
- **`tracker/templates.py`** — The per-form request catalog (FORM_TYPES, FORM_TEMPLATES): what each return type asks for and the keyword rules that recognise each document. The ONLY source of truth for the checklists; the wizard and the rollover read it directly. Since decision 117 it also holds the dates a form implies: FILING_DEADLINES with filing_deadline_for() (the statutory day in the year after the tax year, weekends shifted forward) and ask_by_for() (TARGET_DAYS_BEFORE_DEADLINE before it, moved back off the weekend).
  - constants: `FORM_LABEL_PATTERN` = 'Form {form}', `BASE_YEAR` = 2025, `PERIOD_PATTERN` = 'TY{year}', `K1_CATALOG` = '1040', `K1_IDENTIFIER` = 'F01', `TARGET_DAYS_BEFORE_DEADLINE` = 5, `YEAR_NOTE` = "Defaults to the most recently ended year; the checklist's periods follow it", `KEYWORD_DEFAULT_NOTE` = 'defaults to the document name'
  - imports: `tracker/manifest.py`
  - used by: `tools/backtest.py`, `tools/vocab_report.py`, `tracker/api.py`, `tracker/rollover.py`

  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/samples.py`, `tests/test_api.py`, `tests/test_backtest.py`, `tests/test_catalog.py`, `tests/test_content_check.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_irs_forms.py`, `tests/test_layout.py`, `tests/test_learned_keywords.py`, `tests/test_manifest.py`, `tests/test_real_corpus.py`, `tests/test_rollover.py`, `tests/test_router.py`, `tests/test_row_columns.py`, `tests/test_scaffold.py`, `tests/test_single_source.py`
  - note: item_from_spec() gives a rule-less request its own document name as the required keyword, because a request with no rule can never auto-file, and the safe extension default. default_tax_year() is the calendar's most recently ended year; template_items(form, year=...) shifts the catalog's base year to it, relative periods included. No date_pattern in the catalog: each row's Period implies its year check. Decision 60: a catalog keyword is the form's own title or a phrase only it carries, never a word other forms print about it (a 1040 says W-2; a 1095-C says Marketplace). Decision 62: every catalog row keys on the document's own title phrase; tests/test_catalog.py routes reconstructions of the real forms against every catalog. Decision 63: the prior-year return rows require their form number and title, so a return wins over its schedules' lines. Decision 64: the return rows require their title phrase, not their number; the K-1 row keys on the K-1's title; tests/irs/ (the IRS's own forms) and tests/test_irs_forms.py route them all. Decision 65: every prior-year return row requires the jurat; schedule rows key on their titles, not on account names. Decision 66: no row keys on a line every return prints (dividends and distributions, ownership percentage, donation) or the organizer asks (child care provider); the receipt, list and childcare rows key on those documents' own titles. Decision 67: the receipt row does not key on contribution statement (an IRA's, a 529's); the childcare row knows the provider's statement; the estimated tax row keys on a voucher's own lines (its numbered heading, the amount line), not the booklet's prose. Decision 68: the receipt row keys on receipt wording only (a pledge, a thank-you and the firm's letter are not receipts); the estimated tax row knows the state voucher; the childcare row does not take an FSA administrator's statement. Decision 69: the receipt row keys on words only a charity prints; no form 540-es; L01 has no tuition statement (a checklist's line, a university's bill). Decision 72: item_from_spec() reads a spec's lists through manifest.csv_tuple(), the one parser, rather than a copy of it. Decision 73: the shared estimated-tax row is two rows, because an individual's 1040-ES voucher is not a corporation's record (business_estimated_tax keys on corporation estimated tax, estimated tax voucher, estimated payments made); the December bank row does not key on statement of account (a credit-card issuer's and a broker's heading) and takes a workbook, as the reconciliation it asks for arrives; the property tax row keys on the bill's own titles, not on assessor, parcel number or property tax bill (an assessor's notice and a servicer's escrow analysis print those); D01 drops thank you for your donation (every fundraiser's salutation); I01 drops advance payment of premium tax credit (a marketplace notice's sentence); J01 keys on child care/day care spellings with the run-together copies deleted, since the matcher reads the space as optional; 1041 A01 names the kind of trust (an IRA custodian's paperwork is a Trust Agreement too), B02 drops year-end account statement (a bank's heading), C01 drops distribution schedule (a mutual fund's), E01 knows stepped-up basis; 990 C02 keys on the schedule's own title rather than compensation of officers (Part VII's line and the Statement of Functional Expenses', which is now a financial statement's title), D02 on grants made rather than a bare grantee (a letter the charity received) or grants paid (the 990-PF's line 25), E01 without program description (a grant proposal's); the xlsx-only rows and the loans row take the format a client really sends, and officer_comp drops form 1125-e with it (the blank IRS form parks). Decision 85: 1040 E01 knows the wording a broker actually exports - realized gain/loss and the run-together realized gain loss beside the firm's own realized gain and loss - and takes a workbook, since that export arrives as an .xlsx as often as a CSV; 1041 B01 takes the same two, because the trust's realized gain/loss export is its 1099-B by another name. No IRS form in tests/irs/ says either word, and decision 68's consolidated 1099 never prints them, so the composite's placements are untouched. Decision 90, the owner's catalog: _prior_return() writes every prior-year return row's required keyword, with JURAT as the one owner of the line decision 65 added, and a state return's own printed title as an alternative inside that keyword - a standalone CA 540 or NY IT-201 files 1040 B01 on 'resident income tax return', a CA 568 or NY IT-204 files 1065 A01 on 'return of income + limited liability company' (both 568 heading lines, since decision 141) or 'partnership return', a CA 100S files 1120S A01 on 'franchise or income tax return', and another state is one more phrase, not a rule. The alternative lives inside the required keyword rather than in Any Keywords so the row's required set stays required: the prior-year return still outranks a row that matched on any keyword and one that fails another rule is still contested. The 1040 catalog gains A03-A06, one row per 1099 a person receives, keyed on the form's number - 'nonemployee compensation' is said by the IRS Attention page ahead of every information return and 'certain government payments' by the 1040-ES package, so neither is a keyword; 'miscellaneous information' and 'payment card' are, the second because the 1099-K's title never lands on one line and 'payment card' begins it, where a checklist's menu rule can see it. 'depreciation' joins SHARED - the 1120's C02 unchanged, 1120S F02 and 1065 D02 new - so the schedule behind Form 4562 has one set of words; a fixed-asset register that never says depreciation stays on fixed_assets, which all three catalogs already carry. Decision 93: the catalog keeps ONE K-1 row (1040 F01, K1_CATALOG/K1_IDENTIFIER) and it asks for the state K-1 too - California heads Schedule K-1 (568) "Member's Share of Income" - because which partnerships a client is in is a fact about that client, not about the 1040. issuer_row() cuts a row per issuing entity from k1_row(): same Any Keywords, same period and extensions, the normalised entity name in Required Keywords and in the Document. The 1065's F01 is Special Allocation Support; decision 141's H01 closes decision 85's F1 there. Decision 117, the owner's table: each form's statutory filing date lives here because it is a fact about the return type, like the checklist itself, and a form the table does not name gets no default date at all - a guessed deadline would be read out to a client in the firm's name. The weekend shift is the IRS's own rule; a holiday is a person's edit, because the federal and state calendars differ and move. Every catalog row carries a name mark since decision 128 - 61 of the 107 are named - and an issuer row is named because the K-1 row it is cut from is. Decision 141, the owner's rows: 1040 A07 (SSA-1099 / RRB-1099, required on the statements' own headings so it outranks E02, whose 1099-r the SSA's revision code 'SSA-1099-R-OP1' says), A08, A09, L02, L03 (required on the form number), M01 (the client's Schedule C sheet, any keywords on its own vocabulary) and N01; the business catalogs' K-1s received (required on the partner's, beneficiary's and member's K-1 titles, never the S corporation's, which no business can hold and whose title the S-corp return prints), 1099-K / 1099-NEC received and 1042-S rows; the 1041's G01 carries the estimated_tax title but files only a 1041-ES (an individual's 1040-ES parks there), the one row tests/test_templates.py lets carry a shared title with rules of its own; A08 wants the 1099-C's words beside its number, since OCR reads 1099-G as 1099-C; M01 keys on the summary's shape (gross sales + ending inventory + total expense), never a mileage line; and Z01, the notices row, last on every catalog, keyed on the current IRS notice header (notice date with tax year or tax period, with the agency) and narrow on purpose. The 1042-S, K-1-received, business 1099 and notices rows are SHARED entries. Decision 144: every row carries short= (the owner's approved list of 2026-09-24), as short_title in the spec; a SHARED row has one short name on every catalog; issuer_row() sets manifest.issuer_short_title(), K-1 <issuer> cut to twenty characters at a whole word (the owner's Q-B); ISSUER_DOCUMENT now lives in tracker.manifest (read from there, re-exported here) because the derivation of a blank short name recognises an issuer title and gives a hand-added K-1 row the same name.
- **`tracker/validators.py`** — Tiers 1-2: does the file exist, is the extension allowed, is it big enough, is the PDF readable and - since decision 127 - does the photo open. Pure read-only functions plus passive cloud-placeholder detection for OneDrive and Google Drive.
  - CLI: `python -m tracker.validators`
  - constants: `MAX_READ_MB` = 250, `TEXT_READ_CAP_MB` = 20, `OFFICE_LOCK_PREFIX` = '~$', `PDF_EXTENSION` = 'pdf', `IMAGE_EXTENSIONS` = ('jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'heic', 'heif', 'tif', 'tiff')
  - imports: `tracker/__init__.py`, `tracker/fsio.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/reasons.py`
  - used by: `tools/backtest.py`, `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/router.py`, `tracker/scaffold.py`, `tracker/scanner.py`
  - imports at call time: `tracker/door.py`, `tracker/page.py`, `tracker/scaffold.py`
  - enforces: `rule:no-AI-on-client-documents`
  - tested by: `tests/test_validators.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/child_readers.py`, `tests/test_backtest.py`, `tests/test_content_check.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_fsio.py`, `tests/test_layout.py`, `tests/test_single_source.py`
  - note: DECISION 127 - A PHOTO IS A SCAN: IMAGE_EXTENSIONS (jpg, jpeg, png, heic, heif, tif, tiff) is accepted by every request that accepts a PDF, through extension_allowed() (public since decision 147, for the backtest's collect), so no catalog row and no stored rule changed and a request list recorded before the decision admits photos the day it lands; a row that names an image type itself is taken at its word, and a row listing xlsx/csv alone refuses a photo with the sentence it always refused it with. DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS is untouched. At tier 2 a photo gets from _image_error() what a PDF gets from _pdf_error(): Image.open() + verify(), no pixels decoded, nothing written - a file Pillow will not open is reasons.UNREADABLE_IMAGE (the client's to resend), and a HEIC on a machine whose decoder is missing is reasons.HEIC_NOT_SUPPORTED (firm-side, never an ask: they sent an ordinary photo). pillow_heif.register_heif_opener() runs once at import inside a try, and HEIC_READABLE says whether it did; there is no PdfVerdictCache-style memo because verify() reads a header. Never downloads a cloud-only placeholder — a stub must never be filed as if it were the document. A file that vanishes between listing and stat is reported pending_sync, never raised — a scheduled scan must not die on one replaced file. PdfVerdictCache is a run's memo of PDF readability (the router asks once per manifest row for one file; the scanner asks again): the filer and the scanner each make one and pass it down, so nothing is shared at module level between runs that might one day be concurrent. UNFINISHED_SUFFIXES is the one list of transfer-in-progress names (decision 56). Decision 137 (M5): MAX_READ_MB (250) and TEXT_READ_CAP_MB (20) sit here as constants, not settings; too_large_reason() is what the router and the reader ask before a file is opened. Decision 150 (the review's ruling): open_test(path) is the open test alone, for any row, and it runs in the reading's child; check_file() and check_files() take its verdict as open_test= and open nothing themselves then - only a caller that hands none in (the CLI, a tool) opens the file here.
- **`tracker/view.py`** — The page a person opens: VIEW_FILENAME, regenerated in the engagement folder at the end of every real pass from the readers (load_manifest() for the request rows and their statuses, read_index() for the originals, review.triage() for what each parked file might be), in four sections - Summary, Requests, Index, Needs Review. Owns the file name, the Summary's labels and their meta names, the three words a view's state is said in (CURRENT / BEHIND / UNKNOWN), the chip's label and the button's, render_page(), write_view(), view_state(), read_stamp(), the two row builders (request_row(), index_row()) and the CLI that redraws one engagement and prints its state.
  - CLI: `python -m tracker.view`
  - constants: `VIEW_FILENAME` = 'Status Report.html', `SUMMARY_SECTION` = 'Summary', `REQUESTS_SECTION` = 'Requests', `VIEW_NOTE` = 'This page is regenerated every pass and holds no facts of its own: every value on it comes from the record, the request list and the index.', `LABEL_ENGAGEMENT` = 'Engagement folder', `LABEL_GENERATED` = 'Generated (UTC)', `LABEL_GENERATED_LOCAL` = 'Generated (this machine)', `LABEL_RECORD_DIGEST` = 'Record SHA-256', `LABEL_REQUEST_ROWS` = 'Request rows', `LABEL_INDEX_ROWS` = 'Index rows', `LABEL_PARKED_ROWS` = 'Parked for a person', `VIEW_LABEL` = 'Status report', `VIEW_OPEN_LABEL` = 'Open Status Report', `NEEDS_REVIEW_FIELDS` = ('received', 'original_name', 'pbc_location', 'reason', 'candidates', 'evidence'), `BADGE_CLASS` = 'badge', `NOT_APPLICABLE_CLASS` = 'not-applicable', `NOT_APPLICABLE_SECTION` = '{label} ({n})', `NOT_ASKED_CLASS` = 'not-asked'
  - imports: `tracker/__init__.py`, `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/fsio.py`, `tracker/layout.py`, `tracker/ledger.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/page.py`, `tracker/records.py`, `tracker/review.py`
  - used by: `tracker/api.py`, `tracker/runner.py`
  - imports at call time: `tracker/door.py`
  - writes: `artifact:Status Report.html`
  - reads: `artifact:Status Report.html`, `artifact:_ledger.jsonl`, `artifact:tracker.db`
  - follows: `tracker/reminder.py`
  - tested by: `tests/test_view.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/test_api.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_row_columns.py`, `tests/test_runner.py`, `tests/test_single_source.py`
  - note: Decision 89, stage A step 3, as decision 91 settled it: the owner's rule is that every file staff open only to READ is a web page. IT HOLDS NO FACT, and that is the whole design: no fact is read back - only the stamp in its meta tags, by read_stamp(), for the current / behind / unknown chip - so the one failure every other file must survive costs nothing here. A page whose replace does not land is not replaced, the run carries view_stale and SUCCEEDS, the older page stands and the next pass lands one. Written through manifest.write_text_atomically(); there is no read-only attribute (a browser holds no write lock). On Windows a plain open() read handle still refuses the replace, so view_stale has a real trigger there. Every value goes through page.esc() and the page fetches nothing. The stamp lives in meta tags in the head and read_stamp() reads it with one regular expression - no HTML parser in production. Decision 104: view_state() compares ONE digest - the record's head (ledger.head()) as it was when the page was drawn, against the head now; a rules edit is an event, so an edit moves the head and the page is honestly behind, and the workbook's digest that used to be the second stamp is gone with the workbook. Section headings come from their owners (REQUESTS_SECTION here, filer.INDEX_HEADING, filer.NEEDS_REVIEW) and the review shortlist's sentences from tracker/review.py. Imports downwards only - ledger, manifest, filer, review, page - and only runner and api import it; writing the view is the last thing a pass does. tests/conftest.py draws the page again from the live readers through render_page() after every test and requires the same bytes, with only the clock excluded. Decision 103: this page is where the statuses and the Validation Notes are READ: REQUEST_COLUMNS is the manifest's ten plus the four the record holds, side by side, and a keyword a person's filing taught the row is in Any Keywords beside the ones they typed. Decision 152: the stamp's digest is read BEFORE the rows - _readers() reads ledger.head() first and hands it to _stamp(), for write_view() and render_page() alike - because the page takes no lock and a line appended between the rows and a head read after them would name a line the rows never saw, so view_state() would call a behind page current. Read first, the error runs toward one redraw (BEHIND). A caller handing in items/entries also hands in the head it read before them (head=); the pass hands in nothing (runner.write_view(engagement) reads all three here), so its single reading is unchanged. ledger.read_with_head() is not used: the rows come from the store's readers, not from that read of the file.

### tooling

- **`tools/backtest.py`** — Routes the firm's own already-sorted documents at the office and scores the router against them: the agreement with where a person filed each one, the confusion pairs, the per-row table, the parked and no-text shares, and the time a real pass takes.
  - CLI: `python -m tools.backtest`
  - constants: `SCHEMA_VERSION` = 1, `NEUTRAL_STEM` = 'document', `PARKS` = 'parks', `SLOWEST_COUNT` = 10, `READING_TEXT` = 'text', `READING_OCR` = 'ocr', `READING_IMAGE` = 'image', `HINT_COLUMN` = 'hint', `REPORT_FLAG` = '--report', `EXPECTATIONS_FLAG` = '--expectations', `OUT_FLAG` = '--out', `OCR_FLAG` = '--ocr', `CATALOG_FLAG` = '--catalog', `YEAR_FLAG` = '--year', `REPORT_NOTE` = "How often the router files the firm's own documents where a person already filed them. No file name, no folder name and no word of any document is recorded here.", `BASELINE_NOTE` = "The agreement the firm's own sorted documents scored, measured at the office. No routing change may lower it.", `UNMEASURED_NOTE` = "No backtest has been run against the firm's own documents yet, so there is no agreement to hold a routing change to. Run the backtest at the office and record it.", `NO_BASELINE` = 'No agreement is recorded: the owner has not yet run the backtest at the office. There is no baseline to hold this report to, and an unknown baseline is not a passing one.', `NOTHING_ROUTED` = 'This report routed no document at all, so it cannot be held to the recorded baseline.', `BELOW_BASELINE` = 'Agreement is BELOW the baseline: {agreement} now, {baseline} recorded.', `AT_BASELINE` = 'Agreement holds: {agreement} now, {baseline} recorded.', `RECORDED` = 'Recorded {agreement} over {documents} document(s) in {path}.'
  - imports: `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/router.py`, `tracker/settings.py`, `tracker/templates.py`, `tracker/validators.py`
  - imports at call time: `tests/test_real_corpus.py`
  - writes: `docs/backtest-baseline.json`
  - documented in: `CLAUDE.md`
  - tested by: `tests/test_backtest.py`
  - note: Decision 74. The measure the fifty blank IRS forms and the typed cases cannot be - decision 70's report leaves most keywords and most rows defended by nothing - and the only corpus made of documents a client actually sent. Each document is routed through a hard link (a copy where the file system refuses one) under one neutral name, so the router's by-name fallback can never read the client's name off the file and the score is the routing rules' rather than the firm's naming discipline; the link is the same bytes, so every tier-2 check still sees the real document. A document with no text layer is its own category, because the only evidence left for it would be the name being hidden - unless OCR is allowed, when nothing is handed over and the router does its own reading under its own stricter rule for OCR words. Catalogs are built the way tests/test_irs_forms.py builds them, with the size floor and the year check lifted. Nothing identifying comes back: counts, catalog identifiers and a row's number in the expectations file, never a file name, a folder name below the corpus root or a word of a document; the corpus, its expectations file and the report stay outside the repository and the tool refuses to write into the tree. Decision 127: route_one() also says which of READING_KINDS each document got - text, ocr or image - and the report's timing carries readings_by_kind, so the reader benchmark can say what a photo costs without a folder of text-layer PDFs flattening the number. The rule is unchanged: an image needs OCR_FLAG, exactly as a scan does. Decision 147: collect lists a document wherever the pass would take it - accepted() asks validators.extension_allowed() row by row (a row with no whitelist takes anything), so a photo is on the skeleton wherever a row takes a PDF and a .bmp still is not; no copy of the extension list is kept here.
- **`tools/gpu_pack.py`** — Makes the graphics card pack (decision 169, ruling 2): one flat gpu-runtime folder of the NVIDIA libraries (CUDA 13, cuDNN 9) copied out of an environment holding requirements-gpu.txt, for Build GPU Pack.bat.
  - CLI: `python -m tools.gpu_pack`
  - constants: `PACK_DIR_NAME` = 'gpu-runtime', `REQUIRED` = ('cudart64_13.dll', 'cublas64_13.dll', 'cublasLt64_13.dll', 'cufft64_12.dll', 'cudnn64_9.dll')
  - run by: `Build GPU Pack.bat`
  - tested by: `tests/test_gpu_pack.py`
  - note: The app ships onnxruntime-gpu but not these libraries (about 1.6 GB), so a fresh install stays small and reads on the processor anywhere; the pack is copied beside tracker-api.exe only on a machine with an NVIDIA card. Flat, because onnxruntime.preload_dlls(directory=...) loads each library from one folder by name. A pack missing one of REQUIRED (the libraries ONNX Runtime's CUDA provider loads) is refused, not made. Downloads nothing itself: the batch file's pip does, from the pinned list, when a person runs it.
- **`tools/learned_keywords.py`** — Lists what the staff taught the router: every keyword a person taught one engagement's request that no catalog row with the same identifier and document carries, across every engagement under the clients root, grouped by request row with the number of engagements that typed it.
  - CLI: `python -m tools.learned_keywords`
  - constants: `FLAG_INACTIVE` = 'inactive', `CARRIED_BY` = '{n} engagement(s)', `MISFILE` = 'would misfile: {form} {placement}', `FILES_AS` = 'files as {identifier} in the {catalog} catalog', `PARKS` = 'parks in the {catalog} catalog', `SAID_BY` = 'said by: {forms}', `CUSTOM_ROW` = 'no catalog holds this row', `IN_CATALOGS` = 'in the {catalogs} catalog(s)', `NONE` = '- none'
  - imports: `tools/vocab_report.py`, `tracker/__init__.py`, `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/door.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/registry.py`, `tracker/settings.py`
  - documented in: `CLAUDE.md`
  - tested by: `tests/test_learned_keywords.py`
  - note: Decision 79. A keyword a filing teaches lives in that one engagement's record, so fifty engagements hold fifty private vocabularies and the catalog is the only one tests/test_catalog.py and tests/test_irs_forms.py defend; this is the season's list of candidates to promote. Read-only in the strong sense: no lock is taken, nothing in an engagement folder is written or moved, and a report path inside the repository is refused - an engagement folder name is a client's name and the report names them on request. The engagement's details have recorded the catalog form since decision 86, but this tool does not read it: a row is compared against every catalog holding it and the report says which matched; a row no catalog holds is a custom request, listed apart with all its keywords. An engagement whose record could not be read is a problem line, never a silent skip. It borrows shipped_catalogs() and corpus_documents() from tools/vocab_report.py, so the catalogs it compares against - built through manifest.validated() over template_items() since decision 104 - and the corpus a candidate can be run over are the coverage report's. manifest_rows() reads through manifest.load_manifest(), which is what puts a taught keyword in front of any reader at all.
- **`tools/lockfiles.py`** — The supply-chain lock (decision 191), standard library only: `hash` fills every lock's hashes from PyPI's JSON API, `check` holds the locks to the requirements*.txt pins (every line hashed, no name twice under one marker, the GUI OpenCV in none), `stamp`/`verify` record and compare the locks inside Setup.bat's .venv, `audit` asks OSV about every locked Python and npm package and fails a native engine (NATIVE_ENGINES: pillow, pypdfium2) whose first release newer than the pin is older than STALE_DAYS - measured from the first newer release, not the newest (review S-1).
  - CLI: `python -m tools.lockfiles`
