  - constants: `NPM_LOCK` = 'app/package-lock.json', `STAMP_NAME` = 'tracker-lock.json', `NATIVE_ENGINES` = ('pillow', 'pypdfium2'), `STALE_DAYS` = 90, `GUI_OPENCV` = 'opencv-python', `PYPI_RELEASE` = 'https://pypi.org/pypi/{name}/{version}/json', `PYPI_PROJECT` = 'https://pypi.org/pypi/{name}/json', `OSV_BATCH` = 'https://api.osv.dev/v1/querybatch', `OSV_BATCH_SIZE` = 1000, `NOT_SET_UP` = "The app's private Python is not set up on this computer. Run Setup.bat once (it needs the internet), then start the app again.", `CHANGED` = 'The package list changed since Setup ran on this computer. Run Setup.bat again, then start the app again.'
  - writes: `artifact:.venv/tracker-lock.json`
  - reads: `artifact:.venv/tracker-lock.json`, `requirements.txt`
  - run by: `.github/workflows/audit.yml`, `Setup.bat`, `Start App.bat`
  - tested by: `tests/test_lockfiles.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/test_build.py`, `tests/test_single_source.py`
  - note: hash and audit reach the network; they are a maintainer's and the weekly workflow's commands, never on the app's or the scheduled pass's path, and nothing under tracker/ imports this module (the fourth standing rule; tests/test_lockfiles.py checks). The network is one injectable fetch(url, body), so the tests run on fabricated answers. Rejected: pip-tools and uv pip compile (each re-resolves and would move pins), pip-audit (one more package to lock and trust). verify returns NOT_SET_UP when there is no stamp and CHANGED when a lock or app/package-lock.json differs from it; the CLI prints the sentence and exits 1, which is what Start App.bat shows.
- **`tools/repo_map.py`** — Builds and incrementally updates this map. Derives imports, exports, CLIs, test coverage and hashes from source; merges the curated layer on top.
  - CLI: `python -m tools.repo_map`
  - constants: `SCHEMA_VERSION` = 2, `MAP_INTRO` = 'Read this instead of re-scanning the repository.', `TESTED_BY` = 'tested by', `EXERCISED_BY` = 'exercised by', `NO_TEST_FILE` = 'no dedicated test file', `IMPORTS_AT_CALL` = 'imports at call time', `UNMERGED_ADVICE` = 'Resolve these and `git add` them first', `REQUIREMENTS_FILES` = ('requirements.txt', 'requirements-build.txt'), `NODE_PREFIXES` = ('artifact:', 'rule:')
  - used by: `tools/vocab_report.py`
  - reads: `docs/repo-map.curated.json`
  - run by: `.github/workflows/gate.yml`
  - documented in: `CLAUDE.md`
  - tested by: `tests/test_repo_map.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/test_single_source.py`
  - note: Standard library only. `update` re-parses only files whose SHA-256 changed, and a change to this file forces a full rebuild — new derivation rules must not leave edges typed by the old ones. Test edges are three-way on purpose: `tests` (the test file owning the module by name) is coverage, `exercises` (any other test importing it) is not, and a test importing another test is a plain `imports`. Decision 151: the hash is of the bytes Git commits - git_text_auto_eol_lf() copies the `text=auto eol=lf` rule in .gitattributes, so a CRLF working copy hashes as the LF file CI checks out and `check` only warns about it - and `build`, `update` and `check` refuse while a merge is half-resolved (unmerged_files()), because git ls-files lists an unmerged path once per stage. That refusal is why the resolved files are `git add`-ed before `update`. tools/vocab_report.py hashes its inputs with the same function.
- **`tools/vocab_report.py`** — Generates the vocabulary coverage report: which keyword in each catalog is reached by which IRS form in tests/irs/ or case in tests/test_catalog.py, tested with content_check.says() the way the router reads, and which keywords nothing in the suite defends.
  - CLI: `python -m tools.vocab_report`
  - constants: `SCHEMA_VERSION` = 1, `GENERATED_NOTE` = 'GENERATED by tools/vocab_report.py — do not edit by hand.', `INPUT_PATHS` = ('tracker/templates.py', 'tracker/content_check.py', 'tracker/manifest.py', 'tests/test_catalog.py', 'tests/test_irs_forms.py', 'tests/test_real_corpus.py', 'tools/vocab_report.py')
  - imports: `tools/repo_map.py`, `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/settings.py`, `tracker/templates.py`
  - used by: `tools/learned_keywords.py`
  - imports at call time: `tests/test_catalog.py`, `tests/test_irs_forms.py`, `tests/test_real_corpus.py`
  - writes: `docs/vocab-coverage.json`, `docs/vocab-coverage.md`
  - run by: `.github/workflows/gate.yml`
  - documented in: `CLAUDE.md`
  - tested by: `tests/test_vocab_report.py`
  - note: The map's counterpart for the routing rules (decision 70). `build` extracts the corpus and routes every keyword (about thirty seconds); `check` compares the SHA-256 of its inputs - the catalog, the matcher, the manifest's validation, the cases, the corpus, tests/test_real_corpus.py and this file - so it costs nothing and CI runs it. The committed report reads no client document: the corpus is the IRS's own blank forms and text the suite typed. Decision 71: when TRACKER_REAL_CORPUS names the firm's own redacted documents, `build` reads those too (kind `real`) and the counts name them; that report is a local reading, never the committed one, and `check` refuses a committed report that names them. Decision 73: the workbook cases are read too - as_a_sheet() renders a client spreadsheet's rows the way content_check._extract_xlsx does, so a keyword only a schedule reaches is not reported as unreached. Decision 104: shipped_catalogs() builds each catalog through manifest.validated() over template_items(), the same validation an engagement's create makes, with no temporary file and no store - which is why tracker/manifest.py is one of its inputs and the report was rebuilt with this decision at the same numbers.

### ci

- **`.github/dependabot.yml`** — Dependency updates (decision 191): pip at the root, npm in app/, github-actions, each weekly, each grouped into one pull request with open-pull-requests-limit 2.
  - note: A pip update bumps a requirements*.txt pin and the lock check then fails until a person moves the same pin in its .lock and runs tools/lockfiles.py hash - the intended stop: no hash enters the repository without a person running the tool that fetched it.
- **`.github/workflows/audit.yml`** — The weekly supply-chain audit (decision 191): on a schedule and by hand only, on ubuntu-latest, runs `python tools/lockfiles.py audit` with no install at all.
  - runs: `tools/lockfiles.py`
  - note: Never on a push or a pull request, so it adds no CI to any change (the cost rule). Scheduled workflows run from the default branch. Detection, not prevention: the hashes stop a replaced file; this finds a known advisory in a file we chose, and a stale native engine.
- **`.github/workflows/build.yml`** — Builds the portable package from a `v*` tag and nothing else (decision 191) by running Build App.bat itself on a Windows runner, proves the frozen executable answers in both of its modes, prints the build-info file, zips the package, publishes its SHA-256 beside it and on the run's summary page, and uploads the zip and the .sha256 as the run's artifact for seven days.
  - runs: `Build App.bat`, `api_entry.py`, `tests/samples.py`
  - tested by: `tests/test_build.py`
  - note: Decision 78. It runs the batch file rather than re-implementing the build, because a second copy of the build is the one that drifts; tests/test_build.py refuses a workflow that names PyInstaller, the packager or the copy itself. The batch file pauses for a person at every exit, so it reads one documented switch that skips the waits, named in its own header and set here. The two smoke checks run the frozen executable, not the source: `list` with the shell's two environment variables set, which must answer JSON rather than a traceback on an install with no clients root yet, and one dry pass over a scratch clients root tests/samples.py builds, which walks filing, routing, scanning and drafting. Since decision 169 the root holds a scan only the reader can file (SCRATCH_SCAN), and the step compares the package's engagement line with the source's own dry pass and reads the run log's first line for reader=processor, so a package missing the reader or a model fails here. It installs the tree in the two steps every install makes (R-11): requirements.lock then rapidocr with --no-deps from requirements-nodeps.lock, both hash-checked (decision 191). Where the package landed is read back out of the batch file's own OUT/PLATFORM/ARCH and app/package.json's two names, so no path here is a second copy of one. Not on push: a freeze, an npm install, an Electron download and a few hundred megabytes of artifact are not what a commit should cost. Decision 191: no workflow_dispatch - v* tags are protected, so a package is the build of reviewed code - and a job guard `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')`; the checksum step runs after both smoke checks, and the runbook compares the summary page's hash with certutil -hashfile before a stick is written (transport, not provenance). Its checkout keeps no credentials (F-12).
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — CI: the triggers, the concurrency rule and two jobs that both call .github/workflows/gate.yml — `linux`, a matrix of the floor interpreter and the office's on every pull request and every push to main, and `windows`, the office's interpreter on pushes to main and on pull requests labelled `windows`. It has no steps of its own.
  - calls: `.github/workflows/gate.yml`
  - note: The map check is the point. docs/repo-map.md is what agents read instead of re-scanning, its freshness is guarded by test_the_committed_map_is_current, and this workflow is what makes that guard run without anyone remembering to. Every step always reports, so a stale map and a failing test surface in the same run. Windows is checked because the firm's machine is Windows and the held lock, the atomic replace and the Windows-only tests behave differently there; the python-version lines are pinned to pyproject's floor and to [tool.office] by guards. Decision 78: the matrix carries the interpreter the office runs beside that floor, because the package is frozen on the office's Python and a suite that has never run there proves nothing about it; the rows are written out one at a time rather than crossed so the floor stays one readable literal for the guard that pins it. Decision 122: a Windows minute is billed at twice a Linux one, so the two Windows rows were four fifths of the price of a run, and a series that pushes three to five times per pull request re-ran them every time — while the gate that precedes every push already runs on Windows, so those jobs repeated a check just made. A pull request now runs Linux only; Windows runs on every push to main, where it is the safety net nobody can skip, and on a pull request that asks for it with the `windows` label (`labeled` joins the pull-request triggers so labelling an open one starts the run). Windows on the floor interpreter is run nowhere, because the floor is a language-version check and Linux makes it. The steps moved out to gate.yml in the same decision: a job's own `if:` is evaluated before a matrix is expanded and cannot see the `matrix` context, so this could not be one matrix with a condition on its Windows rows, and two jobs that each wrote the steps out would be two copies of the gate. Windows is now skipped as a whole on a pull request that did not ask - never started, never billed, and reported as skipped rather than as a check that passed. A Windows-only regression in an unlabelled pull request is found by main's run; the gate and the package build both carry a timeout, so a hung job stops costing after it instead of after GitHub's six hours.
- **`.github/workflows/gate.yml`** — The gate's steps, written once: the test suite, the linter, `repo_map.py check`, `vocab_report.py check` and `node --check` on the three Electron files, on whichever runner and interpreter the caller names. Called by both of ci.yml's jobs.
  - runs: `tools/repo_map.py`, `tools/vocab_report.py`
  - called by: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
  - note: Decision 122. `on: workflow_call` with two required string inputs, os and python-version; the job carries timeout-minutes: 30, the ceiling that stops a hung job (the longest job yet measured is 12.5 minutes). It exists because a job's own `if:` cannot see the matrix, which makes ci.yml two jobs rather than one conditional matrix - and the steps written out in each of them would be two copies of the gate, the second one to drift. Its job is named for the runner and the interpreter it was given, so the check names read as they did before the split. Every step after the suite reports whatever the suite did, and keeps its point: a stale map and a failing test are separate problems, and seeing both in one run beats finding the second after fixing the first. Decision 137 (B3): every action is pinned by a full commit SHA with its tag beside it (tests/test_build.py holds every workflow to it). Decision 191: it installs requirements.lock then requirements-nodeps.lock with --require-hashes, using the runner's own pip (no --upgrade pip), caches on the lock files, and its checkout keeps no credentials (F-12).

### desktop-app

- **`app/main.js`** — Electron main process. Spawns the Python API (`-m tracker.api` under the checkout's .venv interpreter, by its full path, or the frozen executable package.json's config.apiName names in the portable build) and relays its JSON to the renderer over IPC.
  - imports: `app/package.json`
  - spawns: `api_entry.py`, `tracker/api.py`
  - launched by: `Start App.bat`
  - tested by: **no dedicated test file**
  - note: This is the cross-language boundary: everything the UI can do is a tracker.api command. The renderer is untrusted here: a command must be in vocab.commands (before the vocabulary arrives, only BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND, pinned to tracker.api.COMMANDS by a guard) with the one argument shape the renderer uses; open-path opens only a path the API reported in state.paths; the tracker's exit code is read, not discarded, and a tracker that outlives TRACKER_TIMEOUT_MS is killed and reported. The window is sandboxed, cannot navigate and cannot open windows. Decision 160: the shell takes app.requestSingleInstanceLock(); a second launch quits before any window is made, and the running one restores and focuses its window on second-instance - two windows were two editors, and the earlier one's save took the later one's back. Decision 176: devTools is off when packaged, and runTracker() serialises the payload before the tracker starts and writes it as UTF-8, which is how tracker.api._read_spec() reads it. Decision 191: from source it runs .venv/Scripts/python.exe (or .venv/bin/python), never a bare python, and answers with the lock tool's NOT_SET_UP sentence when that is missing; in the packaged app Menu.setApplicationMenu(null) runs before the window is made, so no reload, zoom or developer-tools accelerator exists there (E-7). Decision 188 (E-14): learn() keeps each reported path with its kind from vocab.path_kinds, and openPath lstat()s it and opens it only when it is no symbolic link (Node reports a junction as one) and still a directory for 'folder' or a regular file for 'file'; otherwise vocab.shell.not_opened. No path.relative( and no startsWith( (tests/test_layers.py).
- **`app/package-lock.json`**
- **`app/package.json`**
  - used by: `app/main.js`
- **`app/preload.js`** — Context bridge exposing only the calls tests/test_single_source.py checks against main.js.call(args, payload), tracker.open(path) and tracker.pickFolder(). Nothing else crosses.
  - called by: `app/renderer/app.js`
  - tested by: **no dedicated test file**
- **`app/renderer/app.js`** — The desktop UI: the form-type wizard, the request list and the scan results, and (decision 104) the request-list editor - the only place a rule is entered. Talks only to window.tracker from the preload bridge.
  - loaded by: `app/renderer/index.html`
  - calls: `app/preload.js`
  - tested by: **no dedicated test file**
  - note: Every node is built with el() and placed with replaceChildren; there is no innerHTML and no escaper, so a client's file name, a keyword somebody typed into the request list or a folder name is text whatever characters it carries (a guard checks the sinks are absent). Every word it shows or compares comes from the API's vocabulary (applyVocabulary); SCAN_LABEL is the one label it owns. Decision 76: the Needs Review card asks one question of a parked and a set-aside document alike - which request does this belong to - so reviewRow() builds both, and only an open question carries the note box and the button that sets one aside; what a person has set aside is folded under its own count, never removed from the page, because the list is the only way back. Decision 77: renderUnfileList() is the same list for what is already filed - folded away, there for the one row that is wrong - and the function cannot be called after the decision it shows, because the guard on the renderer's vocabulary forbids that word anywhere in the file. Decision 84: the Needs Review card shows the shortlist. renderReview() maps state.review by pbc_location and hands each parked row its triage; reviewRow() puts the shortlist at the head of the picker under the 'suggested' heading, every other request under 'other_requests', and lists the sentence behind each suggestion beneath the row - an <option> carries no second line, and the reason is what is read before anything is picked. The picker starts on the best suggestion, falling back to the router's own first candidate. A parked file the evidence says nothing about shows the vocabulary's nothing_suggested rather than a guess, and a set-aside row is not triaged at all, so it gets no shortlist. Every word of it - the two headings and the File it label as well - comes from vocab; the renderer still types none. Decision 89: a chip beside the engagement's name says whether its own page still describes it. The word and the label are the API's (vocab.view), the chip's class is derived from the word the same way a status chip's is, and the button opens state.paths.view through the same whitelisted opener the Open Status button uses. Decision 91: that button's label is the API's too - applyVocabulary() fills #view-label from vocab.view.open, exactly as it fills the scan button - so the page carries no word for it, and the path it opens is now an .html file the shell hands to the default browser. Decision 104: requestRows() is the one row component - a table of inputs built from vocab.columns (each column's key, header and help; the two numbers as number inputs whose minimum comes from vocab.editor.minimums, the override a pick of vocab.overrides), used by the wizard's custom-request section (three columns, identifiers assigned as rows are added) and by the editor (all ten). openEditor() opens on state.rules - the person's rows as stored, a derived date pattern shown blank, the file types shown as '*' when any - with the engagement's details laid out from vocab.editor.engagement_fields (a text box, a date or a yes/no box for the editable ones, plain text for the rest) and the keywords filings taught shown beside each row as taught (vocab.editor.learned_note), never as typed. pasteRows() appends rows pasted from a spreadsheet by position - tab-separated if any line holds a tab, otherwise CSV through a small RFC 4180 reader, a first line that repeats the headings skipped - and records nothing. saveEditor() is one edit call: a refusal is shown inside the editor with its row and column and the modal stays open; a save renders the state the API returns, closes, and says what changed or that nothing did, with the warnings under vocab.editor.warnings_heading. Every heading, label, hint and button of the editor is vocab.editor's or vocab.columns'; the Check Manifest button and the button that opened the workbook are gone with the workbook. Decision 112: both row builders put the row's sequence number on the <li> (dataset.seq, from state.index[].seq and state.review[].seq) and assignParked(), dismissParked() and unfileDocument() send it back as seq; assignParked's banner shows the API's overrode_shortlist sentence as a warn note beside left_in_review. A refusal goes through refused(): the API's sentence is toasted, the button re-enabled and refresh() re-reads the state, so the card shows the row as the record now holds it. The renderer types no sentence of its own here either. Decision 113: the learned cell is a list rather than a line - learnedCell() draws the API's learned_note and then one span.ed-learned-word per taught keyword, each with its own button.ed-unlearn carrying the identifier and the word - and a click calls the unlearn command, then re-draws only the learned column from the state that comes back (renderLearnedCells), because unlearning is its own event and lands at once while the rows may hold edits the person has not saved. The note area says the API's unlearned_note, and its scan_note under it when the re-scan could not run; the renderer types no word of it. Decision 110: renderMoved() draws #moved-card above the review card from state.moved - one row per moved working copy, its home and where its bytes are now, with restoreMoved (the restore command), keepMoved (assign, with the request the picker was left on and the keyword typed) and reviewMoved (unfile) behind the three buttons, delegated on #moved-list. The picker and the keyword box are shown only where the API said which request the copy's name belongs to (in_request, decision 168), and the picker starts on it; every word is vocab.review_labels', including the word for a copy that is nowhere. Decision 114: renderReview() draws the same queue twice - the list in #review-list and, in #review-deck, one card at a time. renderDeck() builds the deck from state.review in the API's order with the rows a person sent to the back after it (skipped, pbc_locations, dropped as soon as a row leaves the queue), shows the first card, and is called again from every render, so a row filed or set aside anywhere else simply leaves the deck and the total is always the queue's. The card shows the row's reason, the top suggestion's sentence under the list's own 'suggested' heading (or the vocabulary's nothing_suggested), the set-aside sentences, a keyword box and the position line; acceptCard() files to the suggestion the card carries, openCardInList() switches to the list and outlines the row, skipCard() reorders and sends nothing. fileRow() is the one place the assign call is made - assignParked(), acceptCard() and keepMoved() all reach it, and a guard in tests/test_single_source.py keeps it the only one, so Accept and File it cannot drift apart. reviewMode is the person's choice of rendering, read and written in localStorage under REVIEW_MODE_STORAGE_KEY inside try/catch (a blocked store leaves the app on the list); it is a key and not a word, and nothing about the deck is recorded (decision 83). Decision 118: renderReminder()/loadReminder()/drawReminder() are the Reminder card - the record's last word on the draft, the four stages as a toggle coloured from the API's palette, the letter drawn from its own shape with el() (never from the clipboard's markup, which would be an HTML string), Copy for Outlook putting text/html and text/plain on the clipboard with the same words, Approve sending back the fingerprint of the text on screen, and Open the draft file on the path state.paths names. The stage a person picked is the only thing the page holds of its own and is dropped when the engagement changes. It types no colour: every hex it draws with is looked up in vocab.reminder.palette by the key a stage carries, and a guard reads the file for one. Decision 129 added the household card's two feed lines, the editor's feed list with its picker and its warning, and File under another return on both renderings of the queue - every word of it from the API's vocabulary, as always. Decision 160: the editor sends state's list_head with every save, and a Rename fold (renameChoices(), renameRequest()) calls the rename command, renames the row in place, adopts the version the rename returns and keeps what the person typed and not saved. Decision 157: movedRow() draws a gone row (its copy and its original both gone) with the one answer left, Mark <identifier> missing (vocab.review_labels.mark_missing on the .r-withdraw button the filed list uses), and the moved list's click handler sends it to withdrawAnswer(). Decision 189: runScan() shows the reply's pass_warnings and each other return's error, skip and warnings under its own label, in the same banner and the same way as the asked return's warnings, on the skipped and failed paths too. Decision 188: the household card shows the API's pause sentence and, where there is something to accept, the one 'Accept the folder's name' button, which sends accept-folder-name with the seq and scope the card was drawn from; misfits are drawn from the API's 'where' (the path below the root), never worked out here.
- **`app/renderer/index.html`** — Desktop app shell markup: empty placeholders the renderer fills from the API's vocabulary, under a Content-Security-Policy that allows nothing but the app's own files. Since decision 104 it holds the request-list editor's modal (#editor), every label of which the renderer fills, and the Edit Request List button (#btn-edit) that opens it; the min of a number input is never typed here.
  - loads: `app/renderer/app.js`, `app/renderer/style.css`
- **`app/renderer/logo.svg`**
- **`app/renderer/style.css`** — Desktop app styling.
  - loaded by: `app/renderer/index.html`

### root

- **`Build App.bat`** — Builds the portable package: freezes the API with PyInstaller from the committed api_entry.spec inside a virtual environment holding exactly requirements.lock, requirements-build.lock and requirements-nodeps.lock, installed with --require-hashes, packages the Electron shell with @electron/packager, copies the frozen API into resources/ and writes BUILD-INFO.txt.
  - run by: `.github/workflows/build.yml`
  - freezes: `api_entry.py`
  - note: Reproducible from the commit (decision 46): the freeze runs in its own venv because PyInstaller follows optional imports and the machine's Python would otherwise leak unrelated packages into the package (decision 53). The packager runs through its entry script under `node`, not the `npx` shim, for the ampersand reason Start App.bat states; the copy into the package is `robocopy` with its exit code checked and the executable's presence asserted, because `xcopy` gave up on the package's long paths while the script still reported success (decision 53). Guards pin OUT to .gitignore and the resources path to app/main.js. Decision 55: the venv is made fresh each build; no parenthesised value is expanded inside the build-info block. Decision 78: every exit goes through one `:wait` label, which pauses for the person who double-clicked unless TRACKER_BUILD_NONINTERACTIVE is set - the one switch, named in this file's header and read nowhere else, and what lets .github/workflows/build.yml run this file rather than a copy of it. Decision 191: the installs read the locks in hash mode (a replaced file, or a package the locks do not name, fails the build), tests/test_build.py compares BUILD-INFO.txt's freeze with the union of the locks under the build's markers, NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath is set before the first command and robocopy is called by its full path (E-10).
- **`Build GPU Pack.bat`** — Builds the graphics card pack (decision 169, ruling 2): installs exactly requirements-gpu.lock (--no-deps, --require-hashes) into its own environment and runs tools/gpu_pack.py on it.
  - runs: `tools/gpu_pack.py`
  - note: The only reader of the GPU lock (tests/test_build.py). Build App.bat never runs it: the app is one build and the pack an optional folder. Decision 191: hash-checked, NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath first (E-10).
- **`Setup.bat`** — The one-time setup for running from source (decision 191): makes the app's private Python in .venv, installs requirements.lock then requirements-nodeps.lock (--no-deps) with --require-hashes, runs npm ci in app/, and last stamps what it installed with tools/lockfiles.py stamp.
  - precedes: `Start App.bat`
  - runs: `tools/lockfiles.py`
  - note: The machine's own Python only makes the environment and is never installed into, so no other program can break the app or be broken by it. --clear, so a package an older lock named does not survive. The stamp is written last, so a Setup that stopped part-way leaves none and Start App.bat says to run it again. It is where a machine's Python is first asked: the floor check and its 'Install Python <floor>+' sentence are pinned to pyproject.toml's requires-python (tests/test_single_source.py). Sets NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath first and calls where.exe by path (E-10).
- **`Start App.bat`** — Runs the desktop app from source, offline, and installs nothing (decision 191): refuses in one sentence when Setup.bat has not made .venv, when tools/lockfiles.py verify says the lock files changed since Setup ran, or when app/node_modules is missing; then starts Electron.
  - follows: `Setup.bat`
  - runs: `tools/lockfiles.py`
  - launches: `app/main.js`
  - note: Electron is started through its own entry script under `node`, never the `npx` shim: the shim breaks when the folder's path contains an ampersand, which the firm's own checkout does (decision 53). Decision 191 replaced decision 55's install-every-start: a launch that installed ran a package's install code and reached the network at every start, into the machine's own Python. No pip, no npm ci and no npm install appear in it (tests/test_build.py); its not-set-up sentence is tools/lockfiles.py's NOT_SET_UP word for word. It sets NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath before its first command and calls where.exe by its full path (E-10).
- **`api_entry.py`** — PyInstaller entry point: the portable app's one executable, which is the tracker API by default and the scheduled job (tracker.runner.main) when RUNNER_MODE_FLAG comes first.
  - CLI: `python api_entry.py`
  - imports: `tracker/runner.py`
  - imports at call time: `tracker/api.py`
  - run by: `.github/workflows/build.yml`
  - spawned by: `app/main.js`
  - scheduled by: `tracker/scheduling.py`
  - frozen by: `Build App.bat`
  - tested by: `tests/test_api_entry.py`
  - note: PyInstaller needs a real script, not a -m module. Runner mode is dispatched before tracker.api is imported, because the API imports tracker.scheduling whose TASK_NAME needs the product name the Electron shell passes in the environment - and Task Scheduler passes nothing; the job needs neither of the shell's variables. api_entry.spec (committed; reads config.apiName from app/package.json) is how it is frozen. Decision 150: multiprocessing.freeze_support() is the first statement of the main block, so a reading's child - the frozen executable started again by multiprocessing's spawn - runs as the child and never as the API or the job.
- **`conftest.py`** — Puts the repo root on sys.path so tests can `import tracker` without installing the package - explicitly now, beside pyproject's pythonpath, for editor runners and pytest's rootdir detection.
  - tested by: **no dedicated test file**

## Tests, documents and data files with a stated purpose

- **`CLAUDE.md`** — Agent entry point. Says to read the map instead of re-scanning, how to keep it current, and the standing rules that hold across every module.
  - documents: `tools/backtest.py`, `tools/learned_keywords.py`, `tools/repo_map.py`, `tools/vocab_report.py`
  - note: Points at docs/repo-map.md as the first thing to read in a session.
- **`README.md`** — What the system is, how to run each stage, and how to set it up. Who does what is docs/workflow.md.
  - documents: `tracker/runner.py`
- **`docs/ROADMAP.md`** — The build plan, the hard constraints and the decision log. Every component, all built and tested.
  - documents: `tracker/__init__.py`
  - note: The decision log is the record of WHY: read it before changing behaviour that looks arbitrary.
- **`docs/backtest-baseline.json`** — The one number the backtest commits: how often the router filed the firm's own sorted documents where a person filed them, the count it was measured over, and the day it was measured.
  - written by: `tools/backtest.py`
  - note: Decision 74. Owned by tools/backtest.py; `record` writes it and `check` fails a report below it. It ships with no agreement recorded, and `check` then says plainly that the owner has not yet run the backtest at the office and exits 0 - an unknown baseline is never reported as a met one. It holds a number and a date and nothing a client could be read out of.
- **`docs/repo-map.curated.json`** — The hand-written half of this map: roles, notes, artifacts, cross-language hops and the standing rules. Merged on top of the derived facts and never overwritten by a rebuild.
  - read by: `tools/repo_map.py`
  - note: Edit this, then run `python tools/repo_map.py update`. The generated docs/repo-map.json and docs/repo-map.md are NOT edited by hand.
- **`docs/runbook.md`** — The operator's page for one tax season: the designated machine and today's rule that only one may run a clients root, what a person does each morning and on the draft day, what every index reason and validation note means, and the thirty-minute move to another machine.
  - note: Written for a person, not an agent. Roles are docs/workflow.md and the reasons behind the rules are docs/ROADMAP.md; it links to both rather than repeating them.
- **`docs/storage.md`** — The storage plan in prose: the three words (the record, the ledger, the store) and what each means, why the journal syncs with the engagement folder and the database does not, the journal-then-apply order, the schema table, the edit as the event the rules travel in, rebuild as recovery, the check as the gate, what each of the four stages took away, and (decision 107) why the verdict cache is in the store and not in the record.
  - documents: `tracker/ledger.py`, `tracker/store.py`
  - note: Written with decision 101 and finished with 104. It is the page to read before touching storage. The migrations of decisions 102 and 103, which it described step by step, are gone from the tree and from this page; the History section says they existed and where their reading copy is.
- **`docs/vocab-coverage.json`** — The coverage report as data, with the SHA-256 of every input it was built from; `check` and the suite compare against these. Generated; never edited by hand.
  - written by: `tools/vocab_report.py`
- **`docs/vocab-coverage.md`** — The vocabulary coverage report as people read it: the unreached keywords, the keywords reached only by documents that file elsewhere, the rows nothing files into, then every catalog row by row. Generated by tools/vocab_report.py; never edited by hand.
  - written by: `tools/vocab_report.py`
  - note: Rebuilt with `python tools/vocab_report.py build` in the same commit as a catalog, matcher or case change.
- **`docs/workflow.md`** — How the day-to-day workflow runs.
- **`requirements-build.txt`** — What Build App.bat's freeze needs beyond requirements.txt: the pinned PyInstaller. Installed from requirements-build.lock (with requirements.lock), by hash (decision 191).
- **`requirements.txt`** — Runtime and dev dependencies, pinned exactly (a guard refuses a range), including the reader's runtime closure (decision 169) - rapidocr itself is in requirements-nodeps.txt. The human-edited list of direct pins: nothing installs it directly; every install reads requirements.lock, the whole tree by version and by SHA-256 (decision 191).
  - read by: `tools/lockfiles.py`
  - note: requirements-build.txt adds the pinned freezer on top for Build App.bat; api_entry.spec is the committed freeze and app/package-lock.json the committed Electron install, so a build is made from the commit rather than from whatever was current that day (decision 46). olefile (decision 143) reads an Outlook .msg; pinned here and in requirements.lock, and frozen by the portable build. Decision 169 (R-11): rapidocr's metadata asks for the GUI opencv-python, so its real runtime dependencies are listed here with opencv-python-headless, and rapidocr is installed afterwards with --no-deps from requirements-nodeps.lock - by Setup.bat, Build App.bat, gate.yml, build.yml and the README's setup alike (tests/test_build.py pins both steps everywhere). Two pins carry markers: onnxruntime-gpu on Windows and the plain onnxruntime elsewhere (R-11b, CI has no card), numpy 2.5.3 from Python 3.12 and 2.4.6 for the 3.11 floor (R-11a). pytesseract is gone. Decision 191: constraints.txt is gone; four lock files (requirements.lock, requirements-build.lock, requirements-nodeps.lock, requirements-gpu.lock - not mapped, the map takes no .lock files) carry each pin with the hash of every file PyPI publishes for it, and tools/lockfiles.py check (run by tests/test_lockfiles.py) fails when a pin here and its lock disagree. A pin moves here and in its lock together, then `python tools/lockfiles.py hash`.
- **`tests/samples.py`** — The pile of client documents the suite starts from, built from nothing: text_pdf() prints lines to a real one-page PDF, sheet_xlsx() writes rows to a real workbook, and build_samples() assembles the drop folder a client would leave (a duplicate, last year's form, a Word file, a Google Sheets shortcut, a photo, a half-uploaded temp file).
  - used by: `tests/test_api.py`, `tests/test_backtest.py`, `tests/test_build.py`, `tests/test_catalog.py`, `tests/test_containers.py`, `tests/test_content_check.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_locking.py`, `tests/test_ocr.py`, `tests/test_registry.py`, `tests/test_router.py`, `tests/test_runner.py`, `tests/test_vocab_report.py`
  - run by: `.github/workflows/build.yml`
  - note: No fixture files in the repository and no client data, so every test starts from the same pile. It was the marketing demo's sample builder in tracker/api.py; the demo went (decision 41) and the suite still needed the pile. listing_denied() makes a folder really unlistable for the running account, because rglob and os.walk reach the file system by different calls and a monkeypatch of one proves nothing about the other. Decision 73: sheet_xlsx() is how tests/test_catalog.py routes its workbook cases - half of every catalog asks for a schedule a client keeps in Excel, and a sheet is read as rows of tab-separated cells (a phrase across two cells is one phrase, a phrase down two rows is two labels), so typing one as prose would prove the wrong reading. Decision 78: build_scratch_root() assembles the same pile into a whole clients root - one scaffolded engagement with the documents already dropped - which is what .github/workflows/build.yml runs the frozen package over; the fixture lives beside the pile rather than in a tool of its own so there is one pile and not two that drift. It records the engagement through manifest.create_engagement() directly rather than through the suite's helper, because the build workflow imports this module without conftest (decision 104). openpyxl is imported here to WRITE a client's spreadsheet for the suite to read, which is the one use of it the tree keeps. The pile's 'file nobody accepts' is a .bmp since decision 127: it was a .jpg until a photo became a document, and the claim it carries is about a file type no row takes. Decision 143 added cfb_bytes(), a compound-file writer to the letter of [MS-CFB] (version 3, a mini stream, one FAT), and msg_bytes()/msg_storage() over it, so the suite's .msg fixtures are built from nothing - olefile only reads. Decision 169: scanned_pdf() draws lines on a page and saves a PDF with no text layer, and build_scratch_root() drops one (SCRATCH_SCAN, a W-2 whose box labels and figures are drawn as separate lines) so the frozen smoke check proves the package reads.
- **`tests/test_backtest.py`** — Guards the backtest: a document is routed by its text and never by its name, a file with no text layer is counted apart rather than parked, the report and the console carry no file or folder name, the skeleton is blank with the request folder as the hint and is never overwritten, and an unrecorded baseline is said rather than passed.
  - imports: `tests/samples.py`
  - note: Decision 74. The corpus it scores is built with tests/samples.py in a temporary folder, because no client document is in the repository or ever will be. It also pins the two things the hiding rests on: the neutral name reaches no keyword in any shipped catalog, and a whole pass writes nothing under the repository root.
- **`tests/test_build.py`** — Guards what only the build workflow could otherwise discover ten minutes into a release: that it runs the batch file the repository owns rather than a copy of the build, that the switch it sets is the one that batch file reads, that the flags it fires at the frozen executable are flags tracker/runner.py declares, that it passes the two environment variables tracker/settings.py names, and that both workflows quote the one interpreter pyproject.toml writes down.
  - imports: `tests/samples.py`
  - note: Decision 78. It also asserts the fixture: a scratch root is one engagement discovery finds and a whole dry pass walks, because a smoke check over an empty folder proves only that discovery does not crash. Nothing here can prove the package runs - only the Windows runner can. Decision 137 (M5), on decision 191's locks: requirements.lock, requirements-build.lock and requirements-nodeps.lock pin the whole tree the portable build freezes, by hash; the suite holds requirements*.txt to them, "Build App.bat" to installing them with --require-hashes, and every BUILD-INFO.txt under build-portable/dist to freezing nothing else. Decision 191 also: every pip install in every batch file and workflow is --require-hashes from a .lock and none upgrades pip; the build runs from a v* tag only, with a job guard; the checksum step follows the smoke checks and the upload carries the zip and its .sha256; the launcher installs nothing and speaks the lock tool's sentence; every batch file sets NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath first and calls Windows' own tools by path (E-10); every checkout keeps no credentials (F-12); the audit workflow is scheduled, Linux-only and never on a push.
- **`tests/test_containers.py`** — Decision 143's claims: an email, a .msg (written by the suite's own compound-file writer) and a zip are opened and each attachment filed where it belongs with its row naming the container; a loose twin and a re-sent container are duplicates; a pass killed after the writes ends with each attachment once; nothing lands in the client tree; inline pictures and bodies are skipped and named in the opened line; every limit at its edge; locked, damaged and empty containers park; a name cannot leave its folder; an attachment never files into another household and the hand-over refuses it; a dry run writes nothing; the _Opened sweep; the store rebuilds with the new column.
  - imports: `tests/child_readers.py`, `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/samples.py`, `tests/test_content_check.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_scanner.py`
- **`tests/test_learned_keywords.py`** — Guards the learned-keyword report: two engagements that taught one keyword are one row with a count of two, a keyword the catalog already carries is not reported, a hand-added row is a custom row, an unreadable record is a problem line, the default output holds no folder name, nothing under the repository is written and a path inside it is refused, and a keyword an IRS form says is marked as one that would misfile it.
  - imports: `tests/conftest.py`
  - note: Decision 79. The clients roots are scratch trees under tmp_path, built the way tests/test_registry.py builds one: tests/conftest.py's make_engagement() records the shipped catalog through create_engagement() and a keyword_learned event teaches the keyword, so what the report compares is a real record rather than a stand-in. The corpus case reads the fifty IRS forms and takes about half a minute.
- **`tests/test_real_corpus.py`** — The harness for the firm's own redacted documents: every row of the expectations file beside them routed against a shipped catalog the way tests/test_irs_forms.py routes the IRS's forms, and asserted to file where the firm says or to park.
  - imports: `tests/test_scanner.py`
  - used by: `tests/test_catalog.py`
  - used at call time by: `tools/backtest.py`, `tools/vocab_report.py`
  - note: Decision 71. The corpus is outside the repository, in the folder TRACKER_REAL_CORPUS names, and is never committed; with no corpus the routing case skips by name and the harness's own tests - the reading, the routing and the skip - still run on a scratch folder, so the file is exercised on every machine. It owns read_expectations() and real_corpus(), which tools/vocab_report.py imports, so the report and the test cannot disagree about what an expectation means. Decision 74: read_expectations() takes the file's path rather than its folder, because tools/backtest.py scores an expectations file a person keeps wherever they keep it and the contract has to have one reader.
- **`tests/test_repo_map.py`** — Guards the map's trust contract: derived facts come from source, curated judgment survives regeneration, drift is detected, and the committed map matches the tree.
  - note: test_the_committed_map_is_current fails the suite if someone changed code without running `repo_map.py update`.
- **`tests/test_vocab_report.py`** — Guards the coverage report: reach is says(), not a substring; the four headline lists are computed as claimed on small catalogs; the committed report matches its inputs by hash.
  - imports: `tests/samples.py`, `tests/test_catalog.py`
  - note: test_the_committed_report_is_current fails the suite if a keyword, a case or the matcher changed without `python tools/vocab_report.py build`. Decision 73: a workbook case must read the same to the report as to the suite, so the rendering and a real round trip through openpyxl are asserted equal.

## Artifacts (files the system reads and writes at runtime)

- **`artifact:.venv/tracker-lock.json`** — Setup.bat's stamp, inside the checkout's private environment (decision 191): the SHA-256 of each lock file and of app/package-lock.json as they were when Setup installed them. Start App.bat compares it at every launch through tools/lockfiles.py verify and refuses to start, naming Setup.bat, when it is missing or differs. Not client data; .venv is gitignored.
  - written by: `tools/lockfiles.py`
  - read by: `tools/lockfiles.py`
- **`artifact:Prepared/`** — The firm-side working set: renamed copies sorted per request, plus 00 - Needs Review for anything that could not be identified. The client never sees this.
  - written by: `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/scaffold.py`
  - read by: `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/scanner.py`
- **`artifact:Status Report.html`** — The page a person opens (decisions 89 and 91), in the engagement folder beside the record, and the only file there without a leading underscore because it is the one staff are meant to open. One self-contained HTML file - inline style, no image, no font, nothing fetched - with a sticky navigation and four sections: Summary (the record's head, when it was drawn in UTC and in local time, the counts, and the sentence that says it holds no facts of its own), Requests (statuses as coloured badges; since decision 116 the rows set aside as Override.NOT_APPLICABLE are not in the table but folded below it in one page.details() block per year, headed NOT_APPLICABLE_SECTION with the label and the count, dimmed, in the same columns - and Override Reason is a column), Index and Needs Review (the parked rows, each with the shortlist review.triage() computes and one line per set-aside row it names). Every table sorts on a click through a few lines of inline script and is a plain table without it. REGENERATED BY EVERY REAL PASS from the readers, never on a dry run. It HOLDS NO FACT - every value on it is the record's - so no fact is read back (read_stamp() reads only the stamp) and there is nothing on it to edit. The stamp is in meta tags in the head (tracker-record-sha256, tracker-generated and one per Summary field), which view_state() reads with a regular expression; since decision 104 the stamp is the record's head alone, because a rules edit is an event and moves it. A page whose replace does not land - on Windows an open read handle is enough to refuse it - is simply not replaced: the run reports view_stale and succeeds, and the one on disk stays honestly behind. The app says current / behind / unknown beside the engagement's name (tracker.view.view_state) and opens it with the Open Status Report button; `python -m tracker.view <folder>` redraws one.
  - written by: `tracker/view.py`
  - read by: `tracker/api.py`, `tracker/view.py`
- **`artifact:_Opened/`** — What was taken out of the emails and zips a client dropped (decision 143): J Park & Associates/<household>/<year>/_Opened/<container's stem>/<attachment>, layout.OPENED_DIR_NAME, beside the year's returns in the private tree and never in the tree the client is shared. Each file is an attachment's original - its row's pbc_location - written atomically before the container's row exists. Synced like the rest of the private tree, a named exception to decision 107 by the owner's decision of 2026-09-23, because a recovery and a move to another machine must reach it. Skipped by discovery (the underscore), never a return (no journal), outside every return's working set; a file there no row names is a warning every pass and is never re-sorted or deleted.
  - written by: `tracker/filer.py`
  - read by: `tracker/filer.py`
- **`artifact:_ledger.jsonl`** — The engagement's own append-only record (decision 87), in the engagement folder beside the client's files: one JSON event per line, in the order the writers wrote them - what was preserved, filed, parked, called a duplicate, decided by a person, had its bytes recorded, taught a keyword, the statuses each scan applied, and (decision 104) the request list and the engagement's details as the app's editor saved them, one rules_changed event per save carrying exactly what moved. Written only under the engagement lock, with O_APPEND and fsync, one line per event and never rewritten; a torn last line is ignored by the reader and truncated by the next append. Since decision 102 it is the whole of the index, since 103 the whole of the statuses, and since 104 the whole of the person's rules: filer.read_index(), manifest.load_manifest() and manifest.load_engagement_info() all answer from the fold of these lines (through the store, which keeps the fold so no reader pays for it twice), and there is no other copy. Its presence is what makes a folder an engagement (tracker/registry.py). A journal from before decision 104 may carry rules_imported and migrated lines; both are folded and neither is ever written again. A record that does not read as one is refused by name and the line, for every reader. A person never edits it, and `python -m tracker.store <store> check <root>` is how a person checks the database against it.
  - written by: `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/ledger.py`, `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/runner.py`, `tracker/store.py`
  - read by: `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/ledger.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/registry.py`, `tracker/store.py`, `tracker/view.py`
- **`artifact:pass-order.json`** — The pass-order hint (decision 189, PASS_ORDER_FILENAME in tracker/runner.py): beside the store on the designated machine - never under the clients root, and gitignored and outside the build like tracker.db - holding, per household folder name, when it last completed a pass, how many passes running it was not served, and when the last pass started and ended it. Read by run_registry() to take households least recently completed first (a household a pass was killed in goes last) and to name one not served twice running; written whole after the loop and marked as each household starts. A hint, never a record: deleting it resets the order to the walk's and every count to zero, and nothing else reads it.
  - written by: `tracker/runner.py`
  - read by: `tracker/runner.py`
- **`artifact:reminder-draft.txt`** — The drafted chase email, waiting for a person to read, edit and send. Carries a fingerprint so the weekly job can tell whether it has been edited.
  - written by: `tracker/reminder.py`
  - read by: `tracker/reminder.py`
- **`artifact:runs.log`** — The one run log in the clients root (LOG_FILENAME in tracker/runner.py): one summary line per pass, appended by a pass run with the log flag - the scheduled task passes it - never on a dry run, and never read by the system; a person opens it. Since decision 189 a logged scheduled pass first appends a `[stamp] pass started` line, and the next pass reads the log's last 64 KB to say when a start has no summary after it (PASS_DID_NOT_FINISH); each return's warnings are a count, never their words. *(write-only by design: nothing reads it back)*
  - written by: `tracker/runner.py`
  - read by: `tracker/runner.py`
- **`artifact:status.html`** — The practice on one page, in the clients root beside the run log: every engagement with what it owes, the review queue across all of them newest first, and everything that failed. Written by every real pass (STATUS_PAGE_FILENAME in tracker/runner.py) and by the app's own pass; read by a person, who opens it from the clients folder or with the app's Open Status button. One self-contained file - no script, nothing fetched - because it names client files. Never on a dry run. *(write-only by design: nothing reads it back)*
  - written by: `tracker/api.py`, `tracker/runner.py`
- **`artifact:the client's folder for the year`** — Clients/<Household>/<YYYY>/ - where an original rests after the pass moves it out of the inbox, in the tree the client is shared (decision 125). Flat: one folder per year per household, not sorted by return or by request, because the original's resting place is the record's identity for the document and an original moves exactly once.
  - written by: `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/scaffold.py`
  - read by: `tracker/filer.py`
- **`artifact:the household inbox`** — The household's one permanent drop folder, in the tree a client is shared (decision 125) — the only thing they touch. One per household however many returns it has. Their originals end up in the household's folder for the tax year, beside it, still visible to them and untouched; nothing under that tree is ever a record, a lock, a working copy, a draft or a page.
  - written by: `tracker/scaffold.py`
  - read by: `tracker/filer.py`
- **`artifact:tracker.db`** — The store (decision 101): one SQLite file per clients root, on the designated machine's local disk beside the settings file, holding every engagement's requests, statuses, learned keywords, index rows, details and journal events under that root - all folded from each engagement's journal and from nothing else - and, since decision 107, the tier-3 verdict cache (the verdicts and the file memos), which is the one thing in it that is not a derivation of the journal: a rebuild leaves it empty and the next pass reads each document once. NEVER under the clients root and never in an engagement folder - those sync, and a synced database file is a corrupted database file. Written by tracker/store.py, and through it by the filer, the scanner and the manifest's two writes; read, through the store, by every reader of the index, the request list and the details. Disposable all the same - delete it and every fact it held is still in the journals - so it is never backed up, never synced and a person never opens it. One connection per process (connect(), close()), to the file beside the settings file unless TRACKER_STORE names another; the suite sets that per test. At the user_version `tracker/store.py` declares as `SCHEMA_VERSION`, raised by decisions 104 (the workbook's digest column went), 107 (the verdict cache's two tables), 116 (`override_reason`), 117 (the Filing Deadline column) 119 (the `intents` table) and later decisions, 143 the last (the documents' `container` column); a file at any other version is refused by name rather than opened, and an earlier one is deleted and rebuilt from the journals.
  - written by: `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/runner.py`, `tracker/store.py`
  - read by: `tracker/api.py`, `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/registry.py`, `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/review.py`, `tracker/rollover.py`, `tracker/runner.py`, `tracker/scaffold.py`, `tracker/scanner.py`, `tracker/store.py`, `tracker/view.py`

## Rules that cut across the code

- **rule:no-AI-on-client-documents** — No generative AI ever reads a client financial document. Every routing and status decision comes from deterministic rules in the manifest.
  - enforced in: `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/validators.py`
- **rule:nothing-is-ever-sent** — Nothing is ever sent. The system drafts client emails and stops. There is no SMTP, no mail client and no network call in the reminder or scheduling path.
  - enforced in: `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/runner.py`, `tracker/scheduling.py`
- **rule:nothing-is-guessed** — Nothing is guessed. A document is filed only when exactly one request accepts it - or, when one document names several forms as itself, when each of those forms is accepted by exactly one request, or, when a broker's consolidated statement is accepted by several requests, when exactly one of them accepts it for its 1099-B, which then holds the whole statement. Ambiguous, contested and unrecognized files go to 00 - Needs Review for a person - misfiling a tax document is worse than not filing it.
  - enforced in: `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/review.py`, `tracker/router.py`
- **rule:originals-are-never-altered** — Originals are never altered. Files are moved byte for byte under their own names out of Drop files here into the client's folder for the year; all work happens on copies, and every move is recorded in the record.
  - enforced in: `tracker/filer.py`

## Updating this map

```
python tools/repo_map.py update    # after any code change (incremental)
python tools/repo_map.py check     # verify it matches the working tree
```

Derived facts (imports, exports, CLIs, tests, hashes) are parsed from the source — never hand-edit them. Descriptions, artifacts and cross-language hops are curated in `docs/repo-map.curated.json`; edit that file and re-run `update`.
